translations.reference: Liggins followed in his father’s footsteps and entered a career in medicine.
translations.hypothesis: Liggins pursued his passion for medicine and began his career in the field.

translations.source: Ọ zụrụ ọzụzụ dị ka ọkachamara nke nne na-amụ nwa wee malite ịrụ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ọgwụ Ndị Inyom Nke ala Auckland na 1959.
translations.reference: He trained as an obstetrician and began to work at the Auckland's National Women's Hospital in 1959.
translations.hypothesis: She received her training as a professional midwife and began working at the Auckland Hospital for Women in 1959.

translations.source: Mgbe ọ na-arụ ọrụ n'ụlọ ọgwụ Liggins malitere inyocha ọmụmụ nwa akaghị aka n'oge ezumike ya.
translations.reference: While he was working at the hospital Liggins began to investigate premature labor during his spare time.
translations.hypothesis: While working at the Liggins Hospital, he began to investigate the causes of non-traumatic injuries during emergencies.

translations.source: Nlebaanya ya gosiri na e nye homonu, ọ ga-eme ka nkuume nwata dị n'afọ tozuo oke ọsịsọ karịa.
translations.reference: His research showed that if a hormone was administered it would speed up the baby's foetal lung maturation.
translations.hypothesis: The excessive heat can cause dehydration, making the child more susceptible to illness.

translations.source: Xinhua kwuru na ndị nnyocha gọọmenti chọtara igwe 'igbe ojii' na-edokọ etu njem ụgbọelu si gaa na Wenezdee.
translations.reference: Xinhua reported that government investigators recovered two 'black box' flight recorders on Wednesday.
translations.hypothesis: Xinhua reported that government investigators have discovered a "black box" that recorded data from a plane that crashed in Venezuela.

translations.source: Ndị mgba ibe ha mere ihe ndị gosiri nkwanye ugwu nye Luna.
translations.reference: Fellow wrestlers also paid tribute to Luna.
translations.hypothesis: The friends did something that brought joy to Luna.

translations.source: Tọmi Drima sị na "Luna bụ Eze nwaanyị ihe ngabiga oke nke mbụ. Onye nlekwa ọrụ m nke mbụ. Luna nwụrụ n'abalị ọnwa abụọ. Ọ pụrụ iche dị ka ya. Nwaanyị siri ike."
translations.reference: Tommy Dreamer said "Luna was the first Queen of Extreme. My first manager. Luna passed away on the night of two moons. Pretty unique just like her. Strong woman."
translations.hypothesis: "Luna was the first female CEO of the company. She was a strong and capable leader. Luna passed away after a two-year battle with illness. She will be deeply missed."

translations.source: Dọstin "Goldọst" Runnels sị na "Luna na-eme ihe ndị ara ka m...onwere ike karịa... ahụrụ m ya n'anya aga m na atụkwa anya ya... Enwerem olileanya na ọnọ ebe ka mma."
translations.reference: Dustin "Goldust" Runnels commented that "Luna was as freaky as me...maybe even more...love her and will miss her...hopefully she's in a better place."
translations.hypothesis: Dostin "Goldost" Runnels said, "Luna is doing amazing things... I'm so impressed with her and I can't wait to see what she does next... I have no doubt that she will continue to succeed."

translations.source: N'ime mmadụ otu puku na iri anọ tụrụ ụtụ tupu ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị gọọmenti etiti nke afọ 2010, ndị megidere mba Ọstrelia ịbụ obodo kwuuru onwe ya ji pasentị asatọ rịa elu kemgbe afọ 2008.
translations.reference: Out of 1,400 people polled prior to the 2010 federal election, those who oppose Australia becoming a republic grew by 8 per cent since 2008.
translations.hypothesis: In a recent poll of over 1,000 people, a majority expressed support for a referendum on Australia's constitutional status, following a debate that began in 2008.

translations.source: Onye nlekota ala (Caretaker Prime Minister) Julia Gillard kwuru n’oge Kampeenu nke nhoputa ndi ochichi nke goomenti etiti na okwere na Australia kwesiri ibu repoblik ma Eze nwanyi Elizabeth nke abuo chicha.
translations.reference: Caretaker Prime Minister Julia Gillard claimed during the campaign of the 2010 federal election that she believed Australia should become a republic at the end of Queen Elizabeth II's reign.
translations.hypothesis: The Prime Minister of Australia, Julia Gillard, addressed the nation on the occasion of the Queen's 60th anniversary of her reign, highlighting the significant achievements of her government and the enduring legacy of Queen Elizabeth II.

translations.source: 34 nime-otu-nari-nile bu ndi tinyere aka na ntuli aka ahu n’enwe otu uche ahu, n’acho ka Eze-nwanyi Elizabeth II buru onye eze nke ikpeazu nke Australia.
translations.reference: 34 per cent of those in the poll share this view, wanting Queen Elizabeth II to be Australia's last monarch.
translations.hypothesis: Thirty-four of these statues depict women, and one of them is a statue of Queen Elizabeth II, the reigning monarch of Australia.

translations.source: Ka ịtụ vootu nọ na ngwụcha, pasentị iri abụọ na itolu n'ime ndị elebaara anya kwenyere na Ọstrelia kwesịrị ịbụrụ mba nọọrọ onwe ya ngwa ngwa, ebe pasentị iri atọ na otu kwenyere na Ọstrelia ekwesịghị ịbụ obodo nọọrọ onwe ya.
translations.reference: At the extremes of the poll, 29 per cent of those surveyed believe Australia should become a republic as soon as possible, while 31 per cent believe Australia should never become a republic.
translations.hypothesis: In a recent poll, 60% of respondents said that Australia should prioritize its own interests, while 40% believed that Australia should focus on international cooperation.

translations.source: Onye nwebụrụ mgbanye ọlaedo Olympicruru igwu mmiri na nke 100m na 200m ụdị nnwere onwe na ngwụgharị ugboro atọ n'Egwuregwu Commonwealth ahụ, mana n’ihi mkpesa ya, enweela obi abụọ maka ịdị mma nke ahụike ya.
translations.reference: The Olympic gold medalist was due to swim in the 100m and 200m freestyle and in three relays at the Commonwealth Games, but due to his complaints his fitness has been in doubt.
translations.hypothesis: My former swimming coach was a highly successful Olympic athlete, winning three gold medals in the 100m and 200m freestyle events at the Commonwealth Games. However, due to a serious injury, he was forced to retire from competitive swimming.

translations.source: O nwebeghị ike ịn̄ụ ọgwụ ndị ahụ o kwesịrị iji merie mgbu ya dị ka a machibidoro ha iwu site n’Egwuregwu.
translations.reference: He has been unable to take the drugs needed to overcome his pain as they are banned from the Games.
translations.hypothesis: He was not able to take the medication as prescribed by his doctor, as he had not followed the instructions properly.

translations.source: Curtis Cooper, onye ọka mmụta mgbakọ na mwepụ na onye ọka mmụta sayensị kọmputa na Mahadum nke Etiti Missouri, achọpụtala akara praịm kachasị buo ibu ruo ta na Jenụwarị 25.
translations.reference: Curtis Cooper, a mathematician and computer science professor at the University of Central Missouri, has discovered the largest known prime number to date on January 25.
translations.hypothesis: Curtis Cooper, a graduate student in mathematics and a computer science graduate student at the University of Missouri-Rolla, discovered a prime number with a record-breaking number of digits on January 25.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ nyochara nchọpụta ahụ n’iji ngwaike na ngwanrò dị iche iche site na mbido Februarị ma a mara ọkwa ya na Tusdee.
translations.reference: Several people verified the discovery using different hardware and software by the beginning of February and it was announced on Tuesday.
translations.hypothesis: Several people reported the discovery using different devices and methods, starting in early February, and it quickly gained attention on Tuesday.

translations.source: Ụmụ Kọmetị nwere ike ịbụ isi mmalite nnefe mmiri nye ụwa ya na ihe dị ndụ nwere ike ịmepụta ụmụ protiin ma kwado ndụ.
translations.reference: Comets may possibly have been a source of water delivery to the earth along with organic matter that can form proteins and support life.
translations.hypothesis: Microorganisms can be the starting point for the decomposition of organic matter, and the process can create proteins and other essential compounds that support life.

translations.source: Ndị ọka mmụta sayensị nwere olileanya ịghọta ka uwa dị iche iche sị kpụọ, ọkachasị otu ụwa anyị siri kpụọ, kemgbe okwute igwe na ụwa anyị sukọkọ isi n'ote aka.
translations.reference: Scientists hope to understand how planets form, especially how the Earth formed, since comets collided with the Earth long ago.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists have a dream of creating a better world, especially one where our planet is healthy and thriving, as it was before the industrial revolution.

translations.source: Kuomo, onye dị afọ iri ise na atọ, bidoro ọchịchị gọọmenti steeti na mbido afọ a ma binye aka n'ọnwa gara aga n'iwu kwadoro mmekọahụ nwoke na nwoke maọbụ nwanyị na nwanyị.
translations.reference: Cuomo, 53, began his governorship earlier this year and signed a bill last month legalizing same-sex marriage.
translations.hypothesis: Kuomo, a 43-year-old man, was elected governor of the state at the beginning of this year and has been actively involved in promoting inter-party cooperation and dialogue between men and women.

translations.source: Ọ kpọrọ asịrị ndị ahụ "mkparịta ụka ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na nzuzu".
translations.reference: He referred to the rumors as "political chatter and silliness".
translations.hypothesis: He called them "a forum for political debate and discussion."

translations.source: A na-aka na ọ ga-azọ ọkwa onye isi ala n'afọ 2016.
translations.reference: He is speculated to make a run for president in 2016.
translations.hypothesis: This refers to the election of a new governor in 2016.

translations.source: NextGen bụ otu sistemụ FAA na-asị ga-enye ụgbọ elu òhèerè ife site n’ụzọ kara pee mpe ma chekwa ọtụtụ nde galọnụ nke mmanụ kwa afọ na mkpọfụ anwụrụ.
translations.reference: NextGen is a system the FAA claims would allow aircraft to fly shorter routes and save millions of gallons of fuel each year and cut carbon emissions.
translations.hypothesis: NextGen is a proposed system from the FAA that would allow for more efficient and environmentally friendly air travel, while also reducing the number of aircraft accidents by thousands each year.

translations.source: O ji teknụzụ satilaịti dị iche na teknụzụ rada nọ n'ala were enyere ndị na-ejikwa nfegharị ụgbọelu aka ịma ebe ụgbọelu nọ kpọmkwem ma nyekwa ndị ọkwọ ụgbọelu ozi ziri ezi.
translations.reference: It uses satellite-based technology as opposed to older ground-radar-based technology to allow air traffic controllers to pinpoint aircraft with greater precision and give pilots more accurate information.
translations.hypothesis: The use of satellite technology and ground-based radar systems has provided pilots with accurate and real-time information about weather conditions, enabling them to make informed decisions about flight paths and avoid hazardous weather.

translations.source: Anaghị etinyekwasị ihe njem, ma ụgbọoloko elu ala agaghị akwụsị na Wembli, ma ndowe ụgbọala makwa akụrụngwa dowe ma gbakwaa adịghị ebe ahụ.
translations.reference: No extra transport is being put on and overground trains will not stop at Wembley, and car parking and park-and-ride facilities are unavailable at the ground.
translations.hypothesis: There will be no travel restrictions, and the stadium in Wembley will remain open, although there may be some changes to the way people enter and exit.

translations.source: Ụjọ ụbịam ụzọ njem mere na onwere ike ndị egwuregwu ga egwu n'enweghị ndị nkwado ha.
translations.reference: Fears of lack of transportation raised the possibility that the game would be forced to play behind closed doors without the team's supporters.
translations.hypothesis: The lack of proper facilities and support made it difficult for athletes to train and compete effectively.

translations.source: Otu mmụta e bipụtara na Tọzdee n’ime jọnaalụ Sayensi kọrọ na mwube nke otu ụdị nnụnụ ọhụrụ na Agwaetiti Galápagos nke Ikuedọ.
translations.reference: A study published on Thursday in the journal Science reported on formation of a new bird species on the Ecuadorean Galápagos Islands.
translations.hypothesis: A research paper published on Wednesday in the scientific journal "Science" details the discovery of a new species of tortoise in the Galapagos Islands.

translations.source: Ndị nchọcha sitere na Mahadum Princeton dị na mba Amerịka na Mahadum Uppsala dị na mba Sweden kọwara ụdịdị ọhụrụ pụtara na naanị ọgbọ abụọ, ọ bụ ezie na ụkpụrụ a ka e chere na ọ na-ewe oge karịa, n'ihi ọmụmụ n’etiti otu ụdị nnụnụ bụ Dawin Finchi na-ebi otu ebe, Jiospiza Fọtisi, nakwa Kakụtus Finchi si esi bata, Jiospiza konirostrisi.
translations.reference: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden reported the new species evolved in just two generations, though this process had been believed to take much longer, due to breeding between an endemic Darwin finch, Geospiza fortes, and the immigrant cactus finch, Geospiza conirostris.
translations.hypothesis: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden have discovered a new species of beetle, which is unique because it belongs to only two genera, despite the fact that the established classification system suggests that it should belong to more. The new species, Dawin Finchi, Jiospiza Fọtisi, and Kakatus Finchi, are all closely related and share a common ancestor.

translations.source: E nwere ike ịrụpụta ọla edo n'ime ụdị ụdịdị niile. E nwere ike ịpịakọta ya n'ime ụdịdị ndị pere mpe.
translations.reference: Gold may be worked into all sorts of shapes. It can be rolled into tiny shapes.
translations.hypothesis: It can be produced in various forms. It can be described in simple terms.

translations.source: Enwere ike itinye ya n'ime waya girigiri, nke e nwere ike ịghịkọta ma tee ya ihe otite. Enwere ike itisa ya ma ọ bụ rọkụlọ ya n'ime mpempe akwụkwọ.
translations.reference: It can be pulled into thin wire, which can be twisted and plaited. It can be hammered or rolled into sheets.
translations.hypothesis: It could be inserted into a thin wire, which could then be used to attach it to something. It could also be glued or taped into a notebook.

translations.source: Enwere ike ime ya ọ dị oke gịrịgịrị, ma mado ya n'ahụ igwe ọzọ. Enwere ike ime ya ọ dị oke gịrịgịrị ruo na ụfọdụ oge eji ya achọ ọrụ agba ejiri aka tee n'akwụkwọ akpọrọ "akwụkwọ ihe ngosi" mma.
translations.reference: It can be made very thin, and stuck onto other metal. It can be made so thin that it was sometimes used to decorate the hand-painted pictures in books called "illuminated manuscripts".
translations.hypothesis: It can be very long, but it can also be quite short, depending on the specific task. It can be used to create a visually appealing presentation, such as a slideshow or a poster.

translations.source: A na-akpọ nke a PH nke kemịkal. I nwere ike ịme ihe ngosi site na iji mmiri kabeeji na-acha ọbara ọbara
translations.reference: This is called a chemical's pH. You can make an indicator using red cabbage juice.
translations.hypothesis: This is a chemical solution. It can be used to create a cloudy, opaque appearance.

translations.source: Ihu mmanya kabej a na-agbanwe agba dabere na otu kemikal ya si dị asidik maọbụ bezik (alkaline).
translations.reference: The cabbage juice changes color depending on how acidic or basic (alkaline) the chemical is.
translations.hypothesis: The color of a liquid can change depending on its chemical composition, whether it is acidic or alkaline.

translations.source: Nha nke ayọn Hydrogen nọ na kemịkal ọbụla bụ ihe na-egosi ogo pH ya.
translations.reference: The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions in the tested chemical.
translations.hypothesis: The pH scale is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a chemical.

translations.source: Ayọn Haịdrojin bụ protọn anaarala elektrọn ya (ebe atọm Haịdrojin nwere otu protọn na otu elektrọn).
translations.reference: Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them (since Hydrogen atoms consist of one proton and one electron).
translations.hypothesis: A hydrogen atom is a particle that has one proton and one electron.

translations.source: Kpaharia kota nzu abuo ahu kporo-nku onu ma mgbe-ahu, na aka di mmiri ma dikwa ocha, pikoo ha ka ha ghoo boolu.
translations.reference: Swirl the two dry powders together and then, with clean wet hands, squeeze them into a ball.
translations.hypothesis: The old house stood on a hill overlooking the valley, its windows dark and its paint peeling.

translations.source: Mpụta ya na mmiri dị gị n'aka ga-enwe mmekọrịta, nke ga-enye gị mmetụta dị aghaa ma mepụta ihe dị ka ọkpụkpụ mkpuchi.
translations.reference: The moisture on your hands will react with the outer layers, which will feel funny and form a sort of shell.
translations.hypothesis: The interaction with water in your hand will create a connection, resulting in a smooth, polished surface.

translations.source: Ọ fọrọ obere ka ụlọ niile dị n'obodo Harappa na Mohenjo-daro nwee mpochi mmiri, ya na usoro mkpopu kara aka.
translations.reference: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had a flush toilet in almost every house, attached to a sophisticated sewage system.
translations.hypothesis: The buildings in the ancient cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had sophisticated drainage systems and paved streets.

translations.source: A chọtala sistemu nsi fọdụrụnụ n’ụlọ Minoan ndị dị n’obodo Crete na Santorini na Greece
translations.reference: Remains of sewage systems have been found in the houses of the Minoan cities of Crete and Santorini in Greece.
translations.hypothesis: A sophisticated irrigation system was discovered in the Minoan palaces of Crete and Santorini in Greece.

translations.source: Ha nwekwara ụlọ mposi n'Ijipt mgbe ochie, Peshia na Chaịna. N'okpuru ọchịchị ndị Rom, mgbe ụfọdụ ụlọ mposi na-abụkarị otu akụkụ nke ụlọ ọsịsa ahụ ọha ebe ụmụ nwoke na ụmụ nwanyị nọkọtara ọnụ.
translations.reference: There were also toilets in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. In Roman civilization, toilets were sometimes part of public bath houses where men and women were together in mixed company.
translations.hypothesis: They had private houses in Egypt, Persia, and China. Under Roman rule, some private houses were often part of a larger public building, where men and women lived together.

translations.source: Mgbe ikporo mmadu onye no otutu puku maili site n’ebe ino , ihe iji bu igwe satalaiti.
translations.reference: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite.
translations.hypothesis: When a person travels a distance of ten miles from their home, they use a vehicle, such as a car or motorcycle.

translations.source: Satilaịti nọ n'ikuku na enweta oku ma zighachi ya n'ala na ntabi anya.
translations.reference: The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly.
translations.hypothesis: The snake was coiled in the grass, its scales gleaming in the sunlight as it watched its surroundings.

translations.source: E ji ụgbọelu rọkeetị zije satilaịti n'ikuku. Ndị ọka mmụta sayensị na eji igwe nyocha kpakpando afụ ụzọ n'ikuku mpụga ụwa n'ihi na igwe ụwa anyị na arọgharị ụfọdụ ọkụ anyị na ahụ.
translations.reference: The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view.
translations.hypothesis: The rocket soared into the sky, leaving a trail of fire in its wake. Scientists and engineers had worked tirelessly to develop this new type of rocket, which would allow us to explore the vast expanse of space.

translations.source: O na-ewe nnukwu rọketi gafere ụkwụ otu narị n’elu itinye otu satịlaịtị na teliskop n’eluụwa.
translations.reference: It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
translations.hypothesis: He was driving a large truck that had overturned, with a trailer and a telescope on top.

translations.source: Wiilu agbanweela ụwa n'ụdị enweghị atụ. Ihe kachasị ukwu nke wiilu merela anyị bụ na o nyere anyị ụzọ njem dị mfe ma dị ọsịsọ karịa.
translations.reference: The wheel has changed the world in incredible ways. The biggest thing that the wheel has done for us is given us much easier and faster transportation.
translations.hypothesis: The invention of the wheel has revolutionized the world. One of the most significant benefits of the wheel is that it has provided a much easier and more efficient way to travel.

translations.source: O wetegoro anyị ụgbọoloko, ụgbọala na ọtụtụ akụrụngwa njem dị iche iche.
translations.reference: It has brought us the train, the car, and many other transportation devices.
translations.hypothesis: We have a variety of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and various other transportation equipment.

translations.source: N'okpuru ha bụ ụmụ nwamba ha ọkara na-eri anụoriri ha ọkara nke nwere ike isi na oke bekee ruo na ele nakwa mgbada.
translations.reference: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer.
translations.hypothesis: Bene them are their younger siblings, who are constantly playing and enjoying themselves, from morning until night.

translations.source: N’ikpeazụ, e nwere ọtụtụ obere nwamba (gụnyere anụ ụlọ nwamba furu efu) na-eri ọtụtụ obere ụmụ anụmanụ dị ka ụmụ ahụhụ, oke, ngwere, na nnụnụ.
translations.reference: Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds.
translations.hypothesis: Furthermore, there are many small insects (including houseflies) that feed on various small creatures such as aphids, caterpillars, and grubs.

translations.source: Ihe nzuzo nke ọganihu ha bụ gburugburu ebe obibi, ọrụ nwamba niile ji nke na egbochi ịsọmpi ha na ndị ọzọ.
translations.reference: The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
translations.hypothesis: The key to their success lies in their collaborative environment, where everyone works together and supports each other in their individual pursuits.

translations.source: Ọdụm bụ nwamba kachasị emekọrịta n'onwe ha, na-ebi na nnukwu òtù akpọrọ nganga.
translations.reference: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides.
translations.hypothesis: The snakes are the most dangerous creatures, living in large groups in the jungle.

translations.source: Mpako gasị bụ otu ruo atọ ụmụ nwoke tozuru oke metụtaranụ mejupụtara ya, yana ụmụ nwanyị na ụmụ ya dị ọtụtụ dị ka iri atọ.
translations.reference: Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs.
translations.hypothesis: The family consists of approximately three generations, including parents and several children.

translations.source: Ndị nwanyị na-emetụtakarị nke ukwu n’onwe ha, n’ibu otu nnukwu ezinụlọ nke ụmụnne nwanyị na ụmụ nwa nwanyị.
translations.reference: The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters.
translations.hypothesis: Women often experience intense pain during childbirth, leading to the formation of a strong bond between mothers and their daughters.

translations.source: Ezinụlọ Ọdụm na-akpa agwa ka ezinụlọ oke nkịta ọhịa maọbụ nkịta ụlọ, anụ ndị nwere oyiyi dị ịtụ n'anya nye Ọdụm (mana odịghị otu a n'ebe nnukwu nwamba ndị ọzọ nọ) n'omume, ma bụrụ ihe oke iyi egwu nye ihe ọbụla ha na-achụ na nta.
translations.reference: Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
translations.hypothesis: The family of owls is known for its ability to hunt both in the wild and in the home, with owls having sharp eyesight that allows them to spot prey from a great distance.

translations.source: Ome ihe egwuregwu zuruoke nkeoma, agu ahu ga enyili elu (obu ezie na obughi nkeoma), gwuo mmiri, maa-amaa garuo ebe di oke anya ma doo okpukpu ise dika ike mmadu di ike nwere ike ido.
translations.reference: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human.
translations.hypothesis: The most exciting sports event is undoubtedly the marathon, with its long distance and challenging terrain. The runners must endure extreme physical exertion, battling fatigue and the elements to reach the finish line.

translations.source: Agụ nọ n’otu otu (Genus Panthera) dika ọdụm, owuru, na jaguar. Nwamba anọ ndị a bụ naanị ndị nwere ike ime mbigbọ.
translations.reference: The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar.
translations.hypothesis: The cat belongs to the same genus (Panthera) as lions, tigers, and jaguars. These four species are the only ones that can roar.

translations.source: Ụja agụ adịghị ka mgbọpụta n'uju ụja ọdụm, mana ọ dị nnọọ ka okwu e kwuputara n'iti mkpu.
translations.reference: The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
translations.hypothesis: The sound of a drum is not simply a noise, but rather a language expressed through rhythm and beat.

translations.source: Ona amasi Ocelot iri obere umu-anumanu. Ha ga anwuchi enwe, agwo, oke na nnunu ma ha nwee ike. Oka-na-onuogugu anu anumanu nile Ocelot na achu-nta di obere nnukwu karia ka odi.
translations.reference: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is.
translations.hypothesis: The Ocelot is a solitary and elusive animal. It is a nocturnal hunter, and it preys on a variety of animals, including rodents, birds, and reptiles. The Ocelot's coat is typically spotted with black, brown, and yellow, which helps it to blend in with its surroundings.

translations.source: Ndị oke mmụta sayensị cheere na nwamba Oselọt ji isi esochi ma na-achọta anụ ha ga eri, site na ịkpọkwa imi n'ala iji site ebe ha gara.
translations.reference: Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists have discovered that the elusive pangolin is a nocturnal animal that burrows into the ground to hide, and that it uses its strong claws to tear open termite mounds.

translations.source: Ha na-ahụ ụzọ nke ọma n'abalị, ma na ejegharịkwa na nzuzo karịa. Oselọotụ na agwakọta onwe ha na gburugburu ha iji nwude anụ ha na achụ.
translations.reference: They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
translations.hypothesis: They are skilled in legal matters, but they also possess a strong sense of justice and fairness. They use their knowledge and experience to advocate for their clients and to ensure that they receive a fair outcome.

translations.source: Mgbe ọbụla ụmụ obere ihe dị ndụ (obere ọnụ ọgụgụ yiri onwe ha) si na ndị otu ha pụọ (dịka ha gafee ugwu, osimiri, maọbụ gaa n'agwaetiti ọzọ ebe ọ ga-ara ahụ isi laghachi) ha ga-achọta onwe ha na gburugburu di iche ọtụtụ mgbe.
translations.reference: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before.
translations.hypothesis: Whenever a group of young animals (such as siblings or a family) separates (for example, when they are separated by a river, or when one goes to a different area to find food), they will quickly realize that their environment has changed significantly.

translations.source: Gburugburu ọhụrụ a nwere akụrụngwa dị iche ma ndị ịsọmpi dị iche, n'ihi nke a ọnụọgụgụ ọhụrụ ahụ kwesịrị inwe akụrụngwa dị iche maọbụ ihe mmegharị ọzọ ga eme ya ka ọbụrụ onye ịsọmpi dị ike karịa ka ọdịbu.
translations.reference: This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before.
translations.hypothesis: This new vehicle has unique features and a different design, which means that it should have a competitive advantage over existing models.

translations.source: Ọnụọgụgụ nke izizi agbanwebeghị maọlị, ha ka chọrọ ihe mmegharị dịka nke mgbe mbụ.
translations.reference: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
translations.hypothesis: The number of elements has not changed, but they require a different type of interaction, similar to the initial interaction.

translations.source: Ka oge na-aga, dịka gburugburu ha ọhụrụ bidoro mawa ha ahụ, oyiyi ha na ndị ha hapụrụ ebido na-ebelata.
translations.reference: Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population.
translations.hypothesis: As time passes, the new environment gradually takes over, and the old ways of life, traditions, and customs begin to fade away.

translations.source: Mgbe puku afọ maọbụ rịị nde afọ ụfọdụ gasịrị, otu abụọ a ga adị nnọọ iche ruo oke ebe agaghịzị akpọ ha abụọ otu ụdị.
translations.reference: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species.
translations.hypothesis: After a few years, the two individuals will become very different, and they will no longer resemble each other.

translations.source: Anyi na-akpọ usoro a speciation, nke pụtara nguzobe nke ụdị okike ọhụụ. Speciation bụ nsonaazụ a na-apụghị ịgbagha agbagha na akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke evolushọn.
translations.reference: We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
translations.hypothesis: We refer to this process as speciation, which is the formation of new and distinct species. Speciation is a complex process that cannot be fully explained by simple evolutionary mechanisms.

translations.source: Osisi na-eme ikuku oksigin nke mmadụ na-ekuru, ma ha na e kubanye carbon-dioxide nke mmadụ na-ekufu ume (ya bụ, na-ekufu ume).
translations.reference: Plants make oxygen which humans breathe, and they take in carbon-dioxide which humans exhale (that is, breathe out).
translations.hypothesis: Trees produce the oxygen that humans need to breathe, but they also absorb carbon dioxide, which is a greenhouse gas (meaning, it contributes to global warming).

translations.source: Akụmakụ osisi na emepụta nri nke ha site n’anyanwụ site n’aka fotosintesis. Ha na-enyekwa ndo.
translations.reference: Plants make their food from the sun by photosynthesis. They also provide shade.
translations.hypothesis: Plants produce their own food and oxygen through the process of photosynthesis. They also provide shade.

translations.source: Anyị ji osisi eme ụlọ na akwa. Ọtụtụ nri anyị na-eri bụ osisi. Ewepụ osisi, anụmanụ agaghị adị ndụ.
translations.reference: We make our houses from plants and make clothes from plants. Most foods that we eat are plants. Without plants, animals could not survive.
translations.hypothesis: We use grains to make bread and other foods. Many of the foods we eat are made from grains. Without grains, animals would not be able to survive.

translations.source: Mosasaurus bụbu isi n'anụ na-eri anụ n’oge ya, nke a mere na onweghi ihe na-atụ ya egwu, karịa mosasaurs ibe ya.
translations.reference: Mosasaurus was the apex predator of its time, so it feared nothing, except other mosasaurs.
translations.hypothesis: The Mosasaurus was a large marine reptile that lived during the Cretaceous period, and it was one of the largest predators in its environment, far larger than its relatives.

translations.source: Agba ogologo ya bụ nke emejupụtara n'iji ihe karịrị eze dị aguba-nkọ iri asaa, yana òtú òtù mmezi n'elu ọnụ ya, nke pụtara na ọ nweghị ụzọ mgbapụ maka ihe ọ bụla gafere n'ụzọ ya.
translations.reference: Its long jaws were studded with more than 70 razor-sharp teeth, along with an extra set in the roof of its mouth, meaning that there was no escape for anything that crossed its path.
translations.hypothesis: Its long, smooth surface is made of a hard, durable material, and it has no sharp edges or points, making it safe to handle.

translations.source: Onweghị anyị anya, mana ọ dịka onwere ire abụọ. Ọ na eri mbe mmiri, nnukwu azụ, anụ ndị yiri ya, onwekwara ike na eri ụdị nke ya.
translations.reference: We don't know for sure, but it may have had a forked tongue. Its diet included turtles, large fish, other mosasaurs, and it may even have been a cannibal.
translations.hypothesis: We are not identical, but we share common characteristics. We all have two eyes, arms, legs, and a similar body structure.

translations.source: Ọ wakpọkwara ihe ọ bụla banyere n’ime mmiri ahụ; ọbụná nnukwu dainosọọ dị ka T. rex abụghị atụ n’ebe ọ nọ.
translations.reference: It also attacked anything that entered the water; even a giant dinosaur such as T. rex would be no match for it.
translations.hypothesis: I didn't find anything inside the water; instead, I discovered a large, unusual creature like a T. rex, which was not expected to be there.

translations.source: Ka anyị maara nke ọma imirikiti nri ha, ndị Rom nwere oke ha na ihe erimeeri ijuanya ma ọ bụ pụrụ iche, gụnyere ezi ọhịa, piikọkụ, ejula, na ụdị oke akpọrọ dormouse.
translations.reference: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse
translations.hypothesis: Let's familiarize ourselves with the different types of dormice, as the Romans had a wide variety of them, including field mice, voles, and other small rodents.

translations.source: Ihe ọzọ dị iche bụ na ebe ndị ogbenye na nwanyị ahụ riri nri ha ka ha nọ ọdụ n'oche, ndị ọgaranya na-enwe mmasị inwe mmemme oriri ebe ha ga-eri nke ha n'ezumike.
translations.reference: Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals.
translations.hypothesis: Another difference is that the men and women in the group typically eat together, while the men prefer to have their own designated eating area.

translations.source: Ụmụ nri Ndị Rome Ndị mgbe ochie enwughị ike ịgụnye nri ndị batara Yurop site na Amerịka ma ọ bụ Eshịa na narị afọ ndị na-esotenu.
translations.reference: Ancient Roman meals couldn't have included foods that came to Europe from America or from Asia in later centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The Roman diet in ancient times was limited to foods that could be obtained locally from Europe and Africa, and not from America.

translations.source: Na imaatu, ha enweghi oka, nweghi tomato, nweghi poteto, nweghi koko, na onweghi onye Rome mgbeochie deturu anu toro-toro ire.
translations.reference: For instance, they didn't have corn, nor tomatoes, nor potatoes, nor cocoa, and no ancient Roman ever tasted a turkey.
translations.hypothesis: In the market, there were no vegetables, no tomatoes, no potatoes, no beans, and no meat. The people of Rome were very hungry.

translations.source: Ndị Babịlọn rụrụ otu n’ime chi ha otu isi ụlọ nsọ nke e were ka ebe obibi chi ahụ.
translations.reference: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god.
translations.hypothesis: The Babylonians were one of the earliest known religious groups, with their temple as the central place of worship for their gods.

translations.source: Ebe ndị mmadụ wetaara chi ndị ahụ aja, ndị nchụ aja ahụ maka ihe ha bụ chi na-achọ, site n'emume na mmemme di iche iche.
translations.reference: People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals.
translations.hypothesis: People have offered sacrifices to these deities in various ways, depending on the specific deity and the offerings they desired.

translations.source: Ulo-uka n’otu n’otu nwere mbara-ezi ulo-uka ma nwekazie ime ebe nchuaja ebe nani onye-isi nchu-aja nwere-ike ibanye.
translations.reference: Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter.
translations.hypothesis: Each individual house has its own unique design and features, reflecting the cultural traditions and values of the people who live there.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ oge a na arụnye ụlọ elu nwere oyiyi oiramid, ndị akpọrọ ziggurats, ka ha bụrụ osonye ụlọ okpukpe.
translations.reference: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
translations.hypothesis: In some ancient civilizations, temples were built with ziggurats, which were stepped pyramids used as religious structures.

translations.source: Elu ụlọ elu a bụ ebe dị nsọ pụrụ iche nye chi ahụ.
translations.reference: The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
translations.hypothesis: This building is a sacred space dedicated to the deity.

translations.source: Na ekpem-oku nke udidi na mba ndi etiti owuwa-anyanwu, ulo ahu abachaghi uru.
translations.reference: In the warm climate of the Middle East, the house was not so important.
translations.hypothesis: It is a common sight in many African countries, where houses are often built with mud and straw.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ihe ezinụlọ ndị juu a mere, ọ bụ n'anya onye ọbụla ka ha mere ya.
translations.reference: Most of the life of the Hebrew family happened in the open air.
translations.hypothesis: The actions of these families were all individual, and each person acted according to their own beliefs.

translations.source: Ụmụ nwanyị siri nri na mbara eze; ụmụ ụlọ ahịa wụbụ naanị ọgụego mepere emepe na-elefe anya n'okporo ámá. E jire okwute maka ịrụ ụlọ.
translations.reference: Women did the cooking in the yard; stores were just open counters looking into the street. Stone was used for building houses.
translations.hypothesis: The women ate their fill; the shopkeepers only opened their stalls when they saw customers approaching. The market was bustling with activity.

translations.source: O nweghị ụmụ ọhịa buru ibu n’ala nke Keenan, ya mere osisi na-ada oke ọnụ.
translations.reference: There were no large forests in the land of Canaan, so wood was extremely expensive.
translations.hypothesis: The soil in the Keenan area is not very fertile, so the plants do not grow as well.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ anọjughị otu ebe na Grinland. N'akụkọ Norse ha sị na achụfuru Erik the Red n'obodo Iceland n'ihi igbu ọchụ, ma mgbe ọ na aga njem na mgbada ọdịda anyanwụ, ọchọpụtara Grinland wee gụọ ya Grinland.
translations.reference: Greenland was settled sparsely. In the Norse sagas they say that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and when travelling further west, found Greenland and named it Greenland.
translations.hypothesis: The four men never met in Greenland. According to Norse sagas, Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and after sailing west, he discovered Greenland and named it Greenland.

translations.source: Mana n'agbanyeghi nchọpụta ya, agbụrụ Ezkimo ebirilarị ebe ahụ n'oge ahụ.
translations.reference: But regardless of his discovery, Eskimo tribes were already living there at the time.
translations.hypothesis: However, despite this, the Eskimo people had settled in that area at that time.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị na obodo ọbụla bụ 'mba Skandinevia', enwere ọtụtụ ihe dị iche n'etiti ndị, ndị eze, omenala, na akụkọ ihe mere na Denmak, Swiden, Nọọwe na Aisland.
translations.reference: Though each country was 'Scandinavian', there were many differences between the people, kings, customs and history of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Iceland.
translations.hypothesis: Although no single country can be called "Scandinavia," there are many distinct differences between Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Iceland in terms of their people, customs, and history.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ileela ihe nkiri a na-akpọ Akụ nke Mba, i nwere ike chee na e dere otu maapụ akụ n'azụ nke Nkwupụta nke Nnwere Onwe ahụ.
translations.reference: If you have watched the movie National Treasure, you may think a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence.
translations.hypothesis: If you continue reading this work titled "The Soul of the Nation," you may find a map of the country at the end of the book.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị, nke ahụ abụghị eziokwu. N’agbanyeghị na enwere ihe edere n’azụ nke dọkumentị ahụ, ọ bụghị otu maapụ akụ.
translations.reference: However, that is not true. Although there is something written on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map.
translations.hypothesis: That's not true. While there is a map included in the document, it is not a map of the area.

translations.source: Ka-edere na azu nkwuputa nke nnoro-onwe bu okwua “Nkwuputa nke Nnoro-onwe Nke bu ezie ubochi abali 4 juli 1776” .Ederede ahu putara na ala-ala akwukwo ahu, kpodo isi na-ala.
translations.reference: Written on the back of the Declaration of Independence were the words "Original Declaration of Independence dated 4th July 1776". The text appears on the bottom of the document, upside down.
translations.hypothesis: The document is titled "Declaration of Independence, adopted July 4, 1776." It states that these colonies are free and independent states.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ezie na ọnweghị onye maara nke ọma onye dere ya, amaara na mmalite na ndụ ya, afụkọtara nnukwu dọkụment e jiri akpụkpọ anụ mee (o nwere nha inchì 29¾ site na inchì 24½) ọnụ maka nchekwa.
translations.reference: While no one knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its life, the large parchment document (it measures 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was rolled up for storage.
translations.hypothesis: Although the author was not widely known, it was clear from the beginning of his life that he was a gifted writer. He possessed a remarkable talent for using words to create vivid and compelling narratives (with a length of 29¾ inches to 24½ inches).

translations.source: Ya mere, ọ dị ka agbakwụnyere ihe ngosi a dị ka akara njirimara naanị.
translations.reference: So, it is likely that the notation was added simply as a label.
translations.hypothesis: Therefore, it seems like this display is simply being used as a symbolic representation.

translations.source: Ubochi-ubochi nladata ya agha ndi na esota atohapula mpaghara ugwu nke France, mana mpaghara ndida enwerebekwa onwe ha.
translations.reference: The D-Day landings and the following battles had freed the north of France, but the south still wasn't free.
translations.hypothesis: The battle raged across the French countryside, but the determined soldiers fought bravely to defend their homeland.

translations.source: Ndị chịrị ya bụ ndị "Vichy" French. Ndị a bụ ndị mba Frans ndị ha na ndị mba Jamini mere udo n'afọ 1940 ma soro ndị iro rụkọọ ọrụ karịa ịlụso ha ọgụ.
translations.reference: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
translations.hypothesis: The Vichy French were French citizens who collaborated with the Nazi German regime in France during World War II. They chose to cooperate with the Germans rather than resist them.

translations.source: N'ụbọchị nke iri na ise nke ọnwa Ọgọọstụ n'afọ 1940, ndị enyi busoro mpaghara ndịda nke Frans agha, akpọrọ nke a "Operation Dragoon".
translations.reference: On 15 August 1940, the Allies invaded southern France, the invasion was called "Operation Dragoon".
translations.hypothesis: On the 15th of August, 1940, Allied forces launched an offensive in the French region, known as "Operation Dragoon".

translations.source: N'ime nanị izu abụọ ndị agha America na Ndị French nke Nweere onwe ha emeela ka ndịda France nwere onwe ha ma wee na-atụgharị echewe ihu na Germany.
translations.reference: In just two weeks the Americans and Free French forces had liberated southern France and were turning towards Germany.
translations.hypothesis: During the two-year period, American and French forces worked together to liberate France and then turned their attention to Germany.

translations.source: Ọdịnala bụ otu omenaala ọha mmadụ buru ibu na-ebi ma na-arụkọ ọrụ ọnụ, a na-akpọ ọha mmadụ a sosayiti.
translations.reference: A civilization is a singular culture shared by a significant large group of people who live and work co-operatively, a society.
translations.hypothesis: Custom is a long-standing tradition within a particular community, often passed down through generations.

translations.source: Ahịrịokwu "civilization" si n'okwu Latin bụ civilis, nke pụtara "gbasara obodo", nke metụtara okwu Latin bụ civis, nke pụtara onye obodo, na civitas, nke pụtara obodo maọbụ obodo-steeti, nke ahụ nwekwara otu o si egosi nha nke ọha mmadụ.
translations.reference: The word civilization comes from the Latin civilis, meaning civil, related to the Latin civis, meaning citizen, and civitas, meaning city or city-state, and that also somehow defines the size of the society.
translations.hypothesis: The word "civilization" from the Latin word "civilis," which means "belonging to the city," relates to the Latin word "civis," which means citizen, and "civitas," which means city or state. These words reflect the development of human society.

translations.source: Steeti-obodo gasị bụ obu ụzọ nke ụmụ mba. Omenaala kemmepeanya pụtara nnyefe nke ihe ọmụma n'etiti ọtụtụ ọgbọ, akaraụkwụ omenaala nke ka nọ ya na mgbasa dịtụ mma.
translations.reference: City-states are the precursors of nations. A civilizational culture implies the passing on of knowledge across several generations, a lingering cultural footprint and fair dissemination.
translations.hypothesis: A state-owned university is a valuable asset. Its existence represents the transfer of knowledge and expertise from one generation to the next, and it provides a platform for students to develop their skills and knowledge.

translations.source: Ụmụ obere ọdịnala na-apụ n'anya na-ahapụghị ihe akaebe dị mkpa ya mere anaghị ahụta ha dị ka sivilaịzeshọn kwesịrị ekwesị.
translations.reference: Minor cultures often vanish without leaving relevant historic evidence and fail to be recognized as proper civilizations.
translations.hypothesis: Traditional practices that are no longer relevant or necessary are often overlooked and not recognized as important aspects of a community's culture.

translations.source: Ka a na alụ agha ntụgharị, steeti iri na atọ ahụ bu ụzọ gbakọọ bido gọọmenti nchịkọta nke na adịghị ike - nke nzukọ bụ sọ ngalaba onwere- n'okpuru akwụkwọ obodo.
translations.reference: During the Revolutionary War, the thirteen states first formed a weak central government—with the Congress being its only component—under the Articles of Confederation.
translations.hypothesis: During the transition period, the three states were working towards establishing a unified government, but the process was fraught with challenges – primarily due to disagreements between the different regions.

translations.source: Nzukọ enweghị ike ike ụtụ ma n'ihi na enweghi ndị isi ọchịchị gọọmenti etiti maọbụ ndị omeiwu, ọ dabeere na ndị isi ọchịchị steeti, ndị anaghị enwe otu obi ọtụtụ oge ịkwado iwu ya nile.
translations.reference: Congress lacked any power to impose taxes, and, because there was no national executive or judiciary, it relied on state authorities, who were often uncooperative, to enforce all its acts.
translations.hypothesis: The assembly lacked the power to enforce its laws because there were no strong central government or established legal system. It relied on the cooperation of state governors, who were not always willing to uphold its decisions.

translations.source: O nweghi ikike imechi iwu ụtụisi na tarifu n'etiti steeti na steeti.

translations.source: N'afọ 1624, Ụlọọrụ Dọch Isti Indịa mepere ụlọọrụ na ndịda ọdịdaanyanwụ Taịwan, bido mgbanwe n'otu e si emepụta mkpụrụ n'oge gboo, ma wee ndị ọkpọkọọrụ Chaịna ka ha rụọ ọrụ n'ugbo osikapa na nke shuga ha.

translations.source: Na 1895, mgbe a dachara n’Agha Sino-Japanese Mbụ (1894-1895), ọchịchị Qing ahụ mere mbịanye aka na Nkwekọrịta nke Shimonoseki ahụ, site na nke o jiri nyefee Japan ọbụbụeze nke Taiwan, nke na-achị agwaetiti ahụ ruo 1945.
translations.reference: In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
translations.hypothesis: In 1895, following the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing dynasty ceded Taiwan to Japan in the Shimonoseki Treaty, effectively handing over control of the island to the Japanese until 1945.

translations.source: Ndị Ijipt rụrụ n’ime narị afọ atọ BCE, Oke Piramidi ahụ otu n’ime ọtụtụ nnukwu ihe ọwụwụ piramidi arụrụ ịkwanye Fero nwụrụ ugwu.
translations.reference: Built by the Egyptians in the third century BCE, the Great Pyramid is one of many large pyramid structures built to honor dead Pharaoh.
translations.hypothesis: The pyramids were built during the Old Kingdom period of ancient Egypt, around 2500 BCE. The Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the most famous and impressive pyramids ever built, and it was constructed as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu.

translations.source: Ala ugwu Giza maọbụ "Giza Nekropolis" nke dị na ndagwurugwu ọnwụ Ijipt nwere ọtụtụ piramid (nke piramid ukwu bụ nke kachasị ibu), ọtụtụ ebe olili, ọtụtụ ụlọ ofufe nakwa oke Sfinks.
translations.reference: The Giza Plateau, or "Giza Necropolis" in the Egyptian Valley of the Dead contains several pyramids (of which the great pyramid is the largest), several small tombs, several temples, and the great Sphinx.
translations.hypothesis: The Giza plateau, also known as the Giza Necropolis, is located on the west bank of the Nile River in Egypt and contains numerous pyramids (the largest of which is the Great Pyramid), numerous tombs, numerous temples, and the Sphinx.

translations.source: Arụrụ oke piramid iji kwanyere Eze Khufu zugwu, ya na ọtụtụ piramid obere ndị ọzọ, ebe olili na ụlọ ofufe arụrụ ịkwanyere ndị inyom Khufu na ezinụlọ ya ugwu.
translations.reference: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
translations.hypothesis: The massive pyramid was built to house the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu, as well as numerous smaller pyramids, all constructed to house the remains of Khufu and his family.

translations.source: Akara “ụta elu” ahụ yiri otu V ma akara “ụta ala” ahụ yiri otu stepụlụ ma ọ bụ otu ǹkomgbaànoǹhà nke tufure ebe okpuru ya.
translations.reference: The "up bow" mark looks like a V and the "down bow mark" like a staple or a square missing its bottom side.
translations.hypothesis: The "upward pointing" arrow resembles the letter V, while the "downward pointing" arrow resembles a step or a small platform beneath it.

translations.source: Elu pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi n'ọnụnụ ya pịa ụta aka, ma ala pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi na fụrọgụ (nke bụ ebe aka gị ji ụta) were dọọ ụta aka.
translations.reference: Up means you should start at the tip and push the bow, and down means you should start at the frog (which is where your hand is holding the bow) and pull the bow.
translations.hypothesis: This means that you should use your index finger to press the keys on the keyboard, but it also means that you should use your middle finger (the finger you use to type) to press the keys.

translations.source: Otu ụta-elu na -emepụtakarị ụda kara dị nro, ebe ụta-ala ka sie ike ma kara kwupụta.
translations.reference: An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive.
translations.hypothesis: The upper room was dark and quiet, while the lower room was bright and bustling with activity.

translations.source: Detuo akara nke gị na nwere onwe, mana chetakwa na akara ndị ahụ ebiri ebi nwere uru egwu ha bara, n'ihi nke a ha kwesịrị ka akwanyere ha ugwu.
translations.reference: Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected.
translations.hypothesis: Your own unique talents are valuable, but it's also important to recognize that other people have their own strengths and abilities. Therefore, it's beneficial to learn from and appreciate the skills of others.

translations.source: N'Oktoba 6, 1789, ụmụ nwanyị ahịa iwe ji yiri Eze Luwi XVI oke egwu mgbe ha si na Versailles dọrọ ya, nwunye ya Marịa Antwanet, obere ụmụ ha abụọ (Marịa Teriza dị afọ 11 na Luwi-Chals dị afọ anọ), na nwanne nwanyị Eze, Madam Elizabet, dọghachi ha na Parii.
translations.reference: The terrified King Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette their two young children (11 year old Marie Therese and four year old Louis-Charles) and the King's sister, Madam Elizabeth, on the 6th October 1789 were forced back to Paris from Versailles by a mob of market women.
translations.hypothesis: On October 6, 1789, a group of women stormed the Palace of Versailles, confronting King Louis XVI and his family. They included the Queen, Marie Antoinette, their two young children (Marie Thérèse, age 11, and Louis-Charles, age 4), and the Queen's sister, Madame Elisabeth.

translations.source: Ha laghachiri Paris n'ime moto ịnyịnya ndị iwe na-ewe gbara gburugburu, ha na-eti mkpu na-agwa Eze na Nwunye ya ihe egwu dị iche iche.
translations.reference: In a carriage, they traveled back to Paris surrounded by a mob of people screaming and shouting threats against the King and Queen.
translations.hypothesis: They arrived in Paris on a motorcycle, riding through the city's vibrant streets, eager to share their unique performance with the King and Queen.

translations.source: Ndị iwe a manyere Eze na Queen ka ha meghee windo ụgbọ ha.
translations.reference: The mob of people forced the King And Queen to have their carriage windows wide open.
translations.hypothesis: The wind was so strong that it blew the doors of the palace open.

translations.source: N'otu mgbe otu n'ime ndị igwe mmadụ fegharịrị isi onye nche eze egburu na Versailles n'ihu eze nwanyi ụjọ ji.
translations.reference: At one point a member of the mob waved the head of a royal guard killed at Versailles in front of the terrified Queen.
translations.hypothesis: Once, a man in a powdered wig stood before a beautiful woman in a lavish gown in the royal hall.

translations.source: Mmefu ego n'agha nke ndị Amerịka mbịarachịwa na mmeri ndị Filipaị bụ nke ndị Filipino kwụrụ ụgwọ ya n’onwe ha.
translations.reference: The war expenditures of U.S. imperialism in the conquest of the Philippines were paid for by the Filipino people themselves.
translations.hypothesis: The American victory in the Spanish-Filipino War was ultimately achieved through the efforts and sacrifices of the Filipino people themselves.

translations.source: A manyere ha iwu ịkwụ ụtụisi nye ndị ọchịchị mbịarachịwa mba Amerịka iji wedata oke ego e mefuru n'aha gọọmenti mba Filipin site n'aka ụlọakụ Wọlụ Striti.
translations.reference: They were compelled to pay taxes to the U.S. colonial regime to defray a major part of the expenditures and the interest on bonds floated in the name of the Philippine government through the Wall Street banking houses.
translations.hypothesis: A request was made to the American government to provide financial assistance to the Philippine government in order to address the severe economic crisis that the country is currently facing.

translations.source: N’eziokwu, nnukwu uru e nwetara na ogologo mmegbu ndị mba Filipiinụ ga-abụ ihe mejuputara isi uru omume empaya Amerịka.
translations.reference: Of course, the superprofits derived from the protracted exploitation of the Filipino people would constitute the basic gains of U.S. imperialism.
translations.hypothesis: In truth, the long and arduous journey of the Filipino people to achieve independence will undoubtedly serve as an inspiration for future generations.

translations.source: Ịghọta ndị Templars, aghaghi ịghọta ọnọdụ nke kpaliri okike nke otu a.
translations.reference: To understand the Templars one must understand the context that prompted the creation of the order.
translations.hypothesis: Knowing the Templars, it is impossible to understand the circumstances that led to the demise of this order.

translations.source: Ọgbọ ihe ndị a mere na ya ka a na-akpọkarị Ọgbọ Etiti dị Elu bụ oge ihe ndị mere na mba Yuropu n'afọ narị iri na otu, narị iri na abụọ na narị iri na atọ (AD 1000-1300).
translations.reference: The age where the events took place is commonly referred as the High Middle Ages the period of European history in the 11th, 12th, and 13th centuries (AD 1000–1300).
translations.hypothesis: The period known as the High Middle Ages, which spanned from the 11th to the 13th centuries (1000-1300 AD), was a time of significant developments in Europe.

translations.source: Ọgbọ etiti ndị nke mbụ butere ọgbọ etiti ndị dị elu ụzọ, nke ọgbọ etiti nke ngwụcha sotere n'azụ nke gwuru ebe 1500.
translations.reference: The High Middle Ages were preceded by the Early Middle Ages and followed by the Late Middle Ages, which by convention ends around 1500.
translations.hypothesis: The first set of steps led to a higher level, where the final step was located at position 1500.

translations.source: Mkpebi teknụụzụ bụ usoro gazuru nchịkọta nchepụta gasị etinyere n’uju, site na technụụzụ-kwàa maọbụ nye iwu siri ike nke bụ na njedebe nke onye ga-esite n’iwu metụtara sayensi na nke ngosipụta teknụụzụ.
translations.reference: Technological determinism is a term that encompasses a wide range of ideas in practice, from technology-push or the technological imperative to a strict sense that human destiny is driven by an underlying logic associated with scientific laws and their manifestation in technology.
translations.hypothesis: Technological innovation is a process of developing new ideas and inventions, often involving the application of scientific knowledge and technological expertise to create practical solutions.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ nkọwa e nyere nkwenyesiike kenkanụzụ nwere echiche izugbe abụọ: na mmepụta nkanụzụ n'onwe ya na-agbaso usoro nke gbapụrụ iche site na nkwanye nke omenala maọbụ ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị, ya na kwa na nkanụzụ n'aka nke ya nwere "mmekpaahụ" ọ na-enye ọhaobodo nke dị adị, n'abụghị nke sitere na mmekọrịta.
translations.reference: Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that the development of technology itself follows a path largely beyond cultural or political influence, and that technology in turn has "effects" on societies that are inherent, rather than socially conditioned.
translations.hypothesis: Several proposals have been put forward for a more sustainable approach to development, focusing on two key areas: firstly, developing industries that are innovative and distinct from traditional or political interests, and secondly, fostering industries that provide essential goods and services, rather than relying on external markets.

translations.source: Maka ọmụmaatụ, mmadụ nwere ike ịsị na ụgbọala n'ịkwesị ekwesị na-eduga na mmepe nke ụzọ gasị.
translations.reference: For example, one might say that the motor car necessarily leads to the development of roads.
translations.hypothesis: For example, someone might argue that the construction of new roads is essential for economic development.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị nke a, okporo ụzọ zuru obodo ọnụ bụ mmefu ego ma ọbụrụ na ụgbọ ala ehighị nne, ya mere emepụtara ụzọ ọhụrụ ịwedata ego o na ewe inwe ụgbọala.
translations.reference: However, a nationwide road network is not economically viable for just a handful of cars, so new methods of production are developed to reduce the cost of car ownership.
translations.hypothesis: Despite this, the road to the city center is expensive, especially if you are driving a car, so new roads have been built to allow for easier and more affordable transportation.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ mmadụ inwe ụgbọ ala na-ebutekwa nnukwu ihe mberede n'okporo ụzọ, nke na-eweta mmepụta usoro nleta ahụike ọhụrụ maka ịrụzi ahụ mebiri emebi.
translations.reference: Mass car ownership also leads to a higher incidence of accidents on the roads, which leads to the invention of new techniques in healthcare for repairing damaged bodies.
translations.hypothesis: Many people are using vehicles to transport large quantities of waste, which is creating new challenges for waste management and public health.

translations.source: Ihunanya ya nwere otutu ihe banyere mmeme nke ọdịnala, nke sitere n'aka ndị edemede dịka Goethe, Fichte, na Schlegel.
translations.reference: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.
translations.hypothesis: His philosophy was deeply influenced by the classical tradition, drawing on the ideas of figures like Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.

translations.source: Na onodu romanticism, ala ebe onye no bu ihe na kpu omume mmadu, k’oge na aga odinala na omenala metutara ala ebe obibi amalite, nkea mere ndi mmadu jiri nabata odinala na omenala ndia maka na ha na ya bu odinala na omenala nwere nkwekorita karia iwu ana atukwasa n’isi oha.
translations.reference: In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
translations.hypothesis: It is a period of romanticism, when people idealized love and relationships, often ignoring the practical realities of life. This led to a focus on idealized notions of love and marriage, which often clashed with the realities of everyday life.

translations.source: N'otu aka a maara Paris ka isi ejiji ịchọ mma n'ụwa nke oge a, e weere Kọnstantinopul dịka isi ejiji ịchọ mma na mba Yuropu n'oge agha.
translations.reference: In the manner that Paris is known as the fashion capital of the contemporary world, Constantinople was regarded as the fashion capital of feudal Europe.
translations.hypothesis: Considering Paris as the current center of fashion in the world, I would argue that Constantinople (now Istanbul) was the center of fashion in Europe during the time of the Roman Empire.

translations.source: Ebidoro n’afo 400A.D. ruo n’afo 1100 A.D were mara ya na o bu isi mkporindu.
translations.reference: Its renown for being an epicenter of luxury began in about 400 A.D. and lasted up until about 1100 A.D.
translations.hypothesis: The Edo civilization, which flourished between the 4th and 11th centuries AD, was known for its advanced ironworking skills.

translations.source: Ọkwa na gbadara n’oge narị afọ iri na abụọ tụmadị n’ihi eziokwu bụ na Ndị agha ntute alaghachila ma bute ụmụ onyinye dị ka ụmụ akwa sịlk na ngwa nri ndị nwere mbamuru karịrị ihe ahịa Byzantine nyere.
translations.reference: Its status declined during the twelfth century mainly due to the fact that Crusaders had returned bearing gifts such as silks and spices that were valued more than what Byzantine markets offered.
translations.hypothesis: The prevailing theory that the Crusades were primarily motivated by religious zeal and the desire to reclaim Christian lands from Muslim control is largely inaccurate. In reality, the Crusades were driven by a complex mix of factors, including economic interests, political ambitions, and the pursuit of personal gain, such as the acquisition of land, wealth, and power, which often surpassed the religious motivations attributed to them.

translations.source: Ọ bụ n'oge ahụ ka okwa isi ejiji ịchọ ma siri na Kọnstantinopul fere Paris.
translations.reference: It was at this time that the transfer of the title of Fashion Capital from Constantinople to Paris was made.
translations.hypothesis: At that time, the Ottoman Empire was expanding and had conquered Constantinople, which was then renamed Istanbul.

translations.source: Usoro Gotik kasị elu n'oge dị n'etiti afọ ndị nari nke ir na narị nke iri na otu ya na narị nke iri na anọ.
translations.reference: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century.
translations.hypothesis: The Gothic style reached its peak in the 12th and 13th centuries.

translations.source: Na mbido, ọ bụ usoro ejiji ndị Byzantium n'ọwụwa anyanwụ ka onye ọbụla na-eso.
translations.reference: At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east.
translations.hypothesis: Initially, it was a Byzantine military tactic used to encircle and defeat enemies.

translations.source: Mana, n'ihi ụkpụrụ mkparịta ụka na adịghị ọsịsọ, usoro dị na ọdịda anyanwụ nwere ike inọzụga azụ n'oteaka afọ iri abụọ na ise ruo iri atọ.
translations.reference: However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year.
translations.hypothesis: Therefore, due to the lack of proper infrastructure and resources, the development of the eastern region has been slow, with progress only occurring over a period of approximately two to three decades.

translations.source: na njedebe nke oge Mịdụl Eeji ndị ọdịda anyanwụ Europe malitere mepụtawa usoro nke ha. Otu ihe mmepụta kachasi mkpa n'oge ahụ, n'ihi ọgụ aghara, ndị mmadụ bidoro iji bọtịnụ akpọchị akwa.
translations.reference: towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
translations.hypothesis: The beginning of the Middle Ages in Western Europe saw the development of new methods of production. One of the most important innovations of this period was the use of the water wheel, which was used to power a variety of machines.

translations.source: Ugbo oru bu ihe oru ugbo bu nke eweputara iji meputa nri ga ezuru ndi mmadu choro ya ma obu ya na ulo ya.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is agriculture carried out for the production of enough food to meet just the needs of the agriculturalist and his/her family.
translations.hypothesis: A traditional oven is a type of oven used to cook food for a large number of people, either in a communal setting or in a home.

translations.source: Ịkọ ọrụ ugbo bụ ihe dịcha mfe, ọtụtụ mgbe nke ndụ, sistèm n'iji nkpụrụ echekwara bụ nwa afọ na mphaghara ebe obibi ahụ ejikọtara ya na nghagharị mkpụrụ ma ọ bụ usoro ndị ọzọ dị mfe iji mee ka ọmịmị kachasị.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is a simple, often organic, system using saved seed native to the ecoregion combined with crop rotation or other relatively simple techniques to maximize yield.
translations.hypothesis: Gardening is a simple and rewarding activity, often enjoyed by people of all ages and backgrounds. The process of planting and nurturing plants can be a relaxing and enjoyable way to connect with nature and create a beautiful outdoor space.

translations.source: Na mgbe gboo ọtụtụ n'ime ndị na-akọ ugbo na-eme ụdị nke onwe n'enweghị nke orire ọ ka dịkwa otu a n'ọtụtụ obodo ka na etolite etolite.
translations.reference: Historically most farmers were engaged in subsistence agriculture and this is still the case in many developing nations.
translations.hypothesis: Many farmers have been forced to adopt new farming techniques due to the increasing scarcity of water, which is a common problem in many rural areas.

translations.source: Obere omenaala na-ekpọkọta ọnụ ndị nwere ụdị echiche ndị nwere mmetụta na ụkpụrụ keobodo ha leghaara ha anya ma nye ha ohere ịzụlite echiche nke njirimara.
translations.reference: Subcultures bring together like-minded individuals who feel neglected by societal standards and allow them to develop a sense of identity.
translations.hypothesis: The educational program aims to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to develop their own critical thinking abilities and to form their own opinions.

translations.source: Enwere ike imata ngalaba omenala site na afo, agburu, klaasi, ebe onye bi, ma o bu etu chukwu si kee mmadu -i bu nwoke ka ibu nwanyi.
translations.reference: Subcultures can be distinctive because of the age, ethnicity, class, location, and/or gender of the members.
translations.hypothesis: The traditional wedding ceremony can take place in a variety of locations, such as a home, a church, or a hall, and it typically involves a series of rituals and customs that are specific to the Igbo culture.

translations.source: Ihe nlereanya aji ama na omenala pụrụ iche bụ asụsụ, ịchọ mma, okpukpe, ọchịchị, mmekọahụ, ọnọdụ ebe, maọbu njikọ ọtụtụ ihe.
translations.reference: The qualities that determine a subculture as distinct may be linguistic, aesthetic, religious, political, sexual, geographical, or a combination of factors.
translations.hypothesis: The unique and fascinating aspects of Igbo culture include its language, art, music, government, social customs, and its rich history and traditions.

translations.source: Ndịòtù nke otu okpuru omenala na-akpọtụrụkarị ịdị n'òtù ha site n'otu ojiji akanka pụrụ iche ma dịmara, nke gụnyere ụmụ ejiji, omume, na asụsụ ịgba izu.
translations.reference: Members of a subculture often signal their membership through a distinctive and symbolic use of style, which includes fashions, mannerisms, and argot.
translations.hypothesis: The rituals of a particular tribe are often closely linked to their environment, incorporating specific customs, ceremonies, and language related to agriculture and daily life.

translations.source: Otu n’ime ukpuru akacha mara nke atuzi-aka banyere uru di mmekorita bu iweta n’uche ihe nwute banyere umu-aka ndi elefuuru-anya, na-nwuta, maobu mmeto akpachaara-anya mee, enweghi mmekorita ha ndi toro-eto mgbe ha ka na-eto eto.
translations.reference: One of the most common methods used to illustrate the importance of socialization is to draw upon the few unfortunate cases of children who were, through neglect, misfortune, or wilful abuse, not socialized by adults while they were growing up.
translations.hypothesis: One of the most significant challenges in the field of forensic accounting involves dealing with complex financial transactions related to fraud, embezzlement, and other illegal activities. These cases often require a deep understanding of accounting principles, as well as the ability to identify and analyze subtle patterns of deception.

translations.source: Ụdị ụmụaka a ka a na akpọ ndị azụghị azụ. Ọtụtụ ụmụaka an na azụghị azụ abụrụla ndị ndị mmadụ jituru ejitu (ọ na abụkarị ndị mụrụ ha); oge ụfọdụ ngharịpụ ụmụaka bụ maka ọjụjụ ntụpọ dị na ahụ nwatakịrị ahụ a na ahụ anya maọbụ ntụpọ dị n' akọ n'uche ya.
translations.reference: Such children are called "feral" or wild. Some feral children have been confined by people (usually their own parents); in some cases this child abandonment was due to the parents' rejection of a child's severe intellectual or physical impairment.
translations.hypothesis: These types of children are often considered to be "unruly" or "difficult." Many of these children come from disadvantaged backgrounds (often, they are orphans); and at times, their behavior is a result of the trauma they have experienced.

translations.source: Ụmụaka azụghịazụ nwere ike ha e nweela ahụmihe nke mmetọ ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ahụmihe mkpasasị uche nke ukwuu tupu agbahapụ ha ma ọ bụ ha na-agbalaga.
translations.reference: Feral children may have experienced severe child abuse or trauma before being abandoned or running away.
translations.hypothesis: Children with disabilities may experience feelings of isolation or exclusion before or after they are diagnosed, or even while they are still in utero.

translations.source: Ndị ọzọ bụ ebubo ka eboro n’ọbụ ụmụ anụmanụ kpọpụtara ha; a sịkwara n’ụfọdụ biri n’ime ọhịa na onwe ha.
translations.reference: Others are alleged to have been brought up by animals; some are said to have lived in the wild on their own.
translations.hypothesis: The others were simply the result of natural processes; some lived within the soil itself.

translations.source: Mgbe anumanu na-abughi-mmadu zulitechara ya kpam-kpam, nwa-ohia ahu egosi akparama-agwa (na njedebe ebe ana ahu anya) ihe dika nani nke anumanu-nlekota ya, dika ujo ya nye maobu enweghi ujo nye umu mmadu.
translations.reference: When completely brought up by non-human animals, the feral child exhibits behaviors (within physical limits) almost entirely like those of the particular care-animal, such as its fear of or indifference to humans.
translations.hypothesis: As the non-human creature moved stealthily, its eyes (and other senses) registered the presence of a human, causing it to freeze in place, as if it had sensed a threat.

translations.source: Dịka ọmụmụ dabere n’arụmarụ kwesịrị ime ka ọmụmụ kara dị mfe ma na-adọkwu mmasị, ịkụ skafoldu gakwuru otu ụzọụkwụ n’ihu.
translations.reference: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond.
translations.hypothesis: As an example of a design that aims to make learning easier and more engaging, I've created a visual representation of a concept.

translations.source: Skafoldin abụghị usoro mmụta kama ọ bụ enyemaka na-akwado ndị na-amụ ihe ọhụrụ dịka iji program ọhụrụ arụ ọrụ na kọmputa maọbụ ibido ọrụ ọhụrụ
translations.reference: Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project.
translations.hypothesis: A "skaffold" is not a learning method, but rather a tool that supports people who are learning new things, such as how to use new software to perform tasks on a computer or how to start a new business.

translations.source: Ụmụ arụrụmarụ osisi nwere ike ịbụ ma kendịnuche ma ịdịrị ire, n'ụzọ ọzọ, onye nkuzi bụ ụdị arụrụmarụ osisi mana ọ dịkwa dị ka nwoke ntakịrị mkpado akwụkwọ n'ime Microsoft Office.
translations.reference: Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office.
translations.hypothesis: Software applications can be either graphical or text-based. In the first case, the user interface is displayed visually, while in the second case, the user interacts with the program through text commands.

translations.source: A rụnyechara Ihe nkwado n'ime ngwanro a, ndị ga-ajụ ajụjụ, nye ozi, ma kọwaa usoro ndị gaara ara nwa akwụkwọ ahụ ịghọta n'onwe ya.
translations.reference: Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
translations.hypothesis: This chapter provides support for readers, offering questions, information, and methods to help them understand and apply the concepts presented in the book.

translations.source: Enwere ọtụtụ ihe e ji akpọga ụmụ aka ka onye ọzọ lekọta ha, dịka nleghara anya, mmegbu, nakwa nnapụ ihe.
translations.reference: Children are placed in Foster Care for a wide variety of reasons that range from neglect, to abuse, and even to extortion.
translations.hypothesis: There are many ways to discipline a child, such as scolding, punishment, and taking away privileges.

translations.source: Ọ dị mma ka nwatakịrị tolite na gburugburu ebe a na-adịghị elekọta, elekọta, na agụmakwụkwọ, mana ha na-eme ya.
translations.reference: No child should ever have to grow up in an environment that is not nurturing, caring, and educational, but they do.
translations.hypothesis: It's wonderful to see children playing in this safe and supervised environment, with access to toys and educational resources.

translations.source: Anyị na-ahụta Ụkpụrụ Nlekọta anya ahụ ka ebe n’enweghi ihe iyi ndụ egwu nye ụmụaka ndị a.
translations.reference: We perceive the Foster Care System to be a safety zone for these children.
translations.hypothesis: We are observing the lack of opportunities for these children, and it is concerning that there are no resources available to support their development.

translations.source: Ụlọ nchekwa ụmụaka anyị kwesịrị inye ụlọ nwere nchekwa, ndị nledo anya nwere ịhụnanya, nkụzi akwụkwọ dị mma, na nlekọta ahụike dị ntụkwasịobi.
translations.reference: Our foster care system is supposed to provide safe homes, loving caregivers, stable education, and reliable health care.
translations.hypothesis: Our children's daycare should provide a safe environment, caring staff, a good learning environment, and access to healthcare.

translations.source: Ulo nlekọta anya ndi akpotara-akpota kwesiri inyecha ihe nile di mkpa nke na adighi n’ulo ochie esi na kpota ha.
translations.reference: Foster care is supposed to provide all the necessities that were lacking in the home they were previously taken from.
translations.hypothesis: The modern eye examination process differs significantly from the traditional methods used in the past, as it involves more sophisticated equipment and techniques.

translations.source: Ịntanetị na-ejikọ akụkụ nke nkwukọrịta ọha na nkwukọrịta nke mmadụ abụọ.
translations.reference: The Internet combines elements of both mass and interpersonal communication.
translations.hypothesis: The internet connects different parts of the public and private communication networks.

translations.source: Njirimara pụrụ iche nke Ịntaneetị na-eduga akụkụ agbakwụnyere n’usoro nke ojiji ya na usoro afọ ojuju.
translations.reference: The distinct characteristics of the Internet lead to additional dimensions in terms of the uses and gratifications approach.
translations.hypothesis: This unique feature of the internet involves the use of specific algorithms and protocols to manage and control network traffic.

translations.source: Maka ọmụmaatụ, “mmụta” na “mkpakọrịta” bụ ndị atụnyere dịka mkpalite dị mkpa maka ojiji Ịntanetị (James na ndị ọzọ., 1995).
translations.reference: For example, “learning” and “socialization” are suggested as important motivations for Internet use (James et al., 1995).
translations.hypothesis: For example, "learning" and "interaction" are closely related concepts that are essential for the use of the internet (James et al., 1995).

translations.source: Eighmey na McCord(1998) chọpụtara na “nsonye” na “mmekọrịta ga-adịgịde” sokwa na ihe mkpali ọhụrụ mgbe ha nyochara mmeghachi omume ndị na-abịa n'ọtụtụ webụsaịtị.
translations.reference: “Personal involvement” and “continuing relationships” were also identified as new motivation aspects by Eighmey and McCord (1998) when they investigated audience reactions to websites.
