translations.hypothesis: Eighmey and McCord (1998) found that "spam" and "phishing" are new forms of online fraud that exploit users' trust when they analyze the behavior of various websites.

translations.source: Ojiji nke ndekọ vidio edugawo na ụmụ nchọpụta dị mkpa n’ime nkọwa nke nzipụta-n’ihu-kentakịrị, mmegharị ihu nke na-anọru milisekọnd ole na ole.
translations.reference: The use of video recording has led to important discoveries in the interpretation of micro-expressions, facial movements which last a few milliseconds.
translations.hypothesis: The video recording captures crucial details in the process of non-contact measurement, including the movement of the measuring device over a specific time interval.

translations.source: Akachasị ekwu na mmadụ nwere ike ịma mmgbe mmadụ na atụ asi ma ọbụrụ na onwere ike ịkọwapụta obere mmegharị ahụ dị iche iche ọfụma.
translations.reference: In particular, it is claimed that one can detect whether a person is lying by interpreting micro-expressions correctly.
translations.hypothesis: It is important to note that people may have different opinions and perspectives on a particular issue, and it is possible to express these views in a respectful and constructive manner.

translations.source: Oliver Saks, n'akwụkwọ ya Okwu Onyeisi Obodo, gosiri ka ndị enweghị ike ịghọta ọnụ okwu n'ihi isi mmebi nwere ike ikwu mgbe mmadụ na-ekwu eziokwu.
translations.reference: Oliver Sacks, in his paper The President's Speech, indicated how people who are unable to understand speech because of brain damage are nevertheless able to assess sincerity accurately.
translations.hypothesis: In his book, "The Voice of the Silent," Oliver Saks demonstrates how individuals who have experienced trauma may struggle to articulate their experiences accurately.

translations.source: Ọ na-ekwu rịị na ikekwe ụmụ anụmanụ dịka nkịta ụlọ nwekwara ụdịrị ikikere a ịghọta omume mmadụ
translations.reference: He even suggests that such abilities in interpreting human behavior may be shared by animals such as domestic dogs.
translations.hypothesis: He said that the different types of animal sounds, such as the barking of a dog or the meowing of a cat, are all ways that animals communicate with each other.

translations.source: Nnyocha na narị afọ nke iri abụọ egosipụtala na enwere ụdịrị genetik variyeshọn abụọ: nke zoro ezo na nke pụtara apụta.
translations.reference: Twentieth century research has shown that there are two pools of genetic variation: hidden and expressed.
translations.hypothesis: Research over two decades has revealed two types of genetic variation: one that is inherited, and one that arises spontaneously.

translations.source: Mgbanwe n'ọdịdị na-agbakwunye ọdịdị kejenetiki ọhụrụ, ma nhọpụta na-ewepụ ya n'ogwu ọdịdị nke a kọwapụtara.
translations.reference: Mutation adds new genetic variation, and selection removes it from the pool of expressed variation.
translations.hypothesis: The changes introduce new levels of complexity, and the patterns that emerge from these changes are fascinating.

translations.source: Nkewa na ntughari nkpokorita nkeghari na azu n'etiti ọdọ mmiri abua ahu na ọgbọ o bula.
translations.reference: Segregation and recombination shuffle variation back and forth between the two pools with each generation.
translations.hypothesis: The small, rocky outcrop was located in the middle of the stream, between the two banks.

translations.source: N'ime savanna, ọ bụ ihe siri ike na primate nwere usoro nri dị ka nke mmadụ iji mejupụta amino-acid chọrọ site na ihe ọkụkụ dịnụ.
translations.reference: Out on the savanna, it is hard for a primate with a digestive system like that of humans to satisfy its amino-acid requirements from available plant resources.
translations.hypothesis: In the savanna, it is common for primates to have a diet similar to that of humans, using their teeth to grind down tough plant matter in order to extract the amino acids they need.

translations.source: Ọzọ dịka ibe ya, ị jụ ime ihe a nwere nnukwu ntaramahụhụ: nnukwu ndamụmbà, ọtịtaahụ, nakwa ọnwụ n'ikpeazụ.
translations.reference: Moreover, failure to do so has serious consequences: growth depression, malnutrition, and ultimately death.
translations.hypothesis: Like its surroundings, this place is filled with a sense of unease: a heavy atmosphere, a feeling of oppression, and ultimately, a sense of impending doom.

translations.source: Ihe akụrụngwa a na-enweta ngwa ngwa ga-abụrịrị protein ndị dị na akwụkwọ na legume gasị, mana ihe ndị a siri ike maka ndị nyiri mmadụ ndịọzọ bị n’ọhịa dịka anyị iji gbazèe ma anyị sie ya n’ọkụ.
translations.reference: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest unless they are cooked.
translations.hypothesis: This type of protein, which comes from both grains and legumes, is relatively easy to digest for people with digestive issues like ours. We can also easily prepare it at home.

translations.source: N’aka ọzọ, nri anụmanụ arụrụ, ntanta, akwa) abughi naani di nfe, kama ha na-enye oke protein nke nwere amino acid nile di nma.
translations.reference: In contrast, animal foods (ants, termites, eggs) not only are easily digestible, but they provide high-quantity proteins that contain all the essential amino acids.
translations.hypothesis: In addition to being delicious, meat (beef, chicken, fish) is a good source of protein, containing all the essential amino acids.

translations.source: Eleghị anya, ya atụla anyị n'anya ma ọbụrụ na ndị nna nna anyi ji aka ha gboo "mkpa protin" ha n'usoro dị ka nke enwe bi n'ọhịa si eme taa.
translations.reference: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
translations.hypothesis: He clearly understood our concerns and suggested a solution that would allow us to meet our protein needs in a way that was both healthy and convenient, similar to the pre-packaged meals that are now widely available.

translations.source: Nkwụsịtụ ụra bụ usoro nke ịkpacharanya eteta ụra mgbe oge ị na-ehikarị ụra ma na-ada n’ụra mgbe obere oge gachara (nkeji 10–60).
translations.reference: Sleep interruption is the process of purposefully awakening during your normal sleep period and falling asleep a short time later (10–60 minutes).
translations.hypothesis: The weaning process is the gradual transition from breast milk to solid foods, typically starting around 6 months of age and continuing for several years.

translations.source: Enwere ike ime ka n’uzo mfe site na iweta atanu ogbu-opi uzu ya dikariri nwayo ikpobata gi na uche kama ghara ikpotecha gi na-ozuzuoke.
translations.reference: This can be easily done by using a relatively quiet alarm clock to bring you to consciousness without fully waking you.
translations.hypothesis: It felt like a sudden, sharp pain in my stomach, followed by a wave of nausea and dizziness.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị hụtara onwe gị na-ewubergharị elekere gị n’ime nrọ gị, e nwere ike idobe ya n’akụkụ nke ọzọ nke ime ụlọ ahụ, na-amanye gị isi n’akwa bilie ịgbanyụ ya.
translations.reference: If you find yourself resetting the clock in your sleep, it can be placed on the other side of the room, forcing you to get out of bed to turn it off.
translations.hypothesis: If you find that your bed is not providing adequate support, you can try moving it to a different part of the room, or adding a mattress to make it more comfortable.

translations.source: Ụzọ biorhythm ndị ọzọ gụnyere ịñụ oke ihe mmiri (karịsịa mmiri maọbụ tii, dayuretik a maara amaara) tupu arahụ ụra, na-amanye mmadụ ibili maka ịnyụ amịrị.
translations.reference: Other biorhythm-based options involve drinking lots of fluid (particularly water or tea, a known diuretic) prior to sleep, forcing one to get up to urinate.
translations.hypothesis: Other biorhythms include excessive fluid intake (especially water or diuretics), which can lead to dehydration.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ole udo nke obi mmadụ nwere na-emekọrịta na nchịkọta ihu na ole obimgbalielu nọ n'ime ahụ na mmụọ nke mmadụ.
translations.reference: The amount of inner peace a person possesses correlates oppositely to the amount of tension in one’s body and spirit.
translations.hypothesis: What is the nature of human consciousness and how does it interact with the physical world?

translations.source: Ka a na-ewetulata esemokwu ahụ, ka ike ndụ nọ ugbu a na-adịkwuo mma. Mmadu niile nwere ike mmepụta ịchọta udo zuru oke na afọ ojuju.
translations.reference: The lower the tension, the more positive the life force present. Every person has the potential to find absolute peace and contentment.
translations.hypothesis: As we enjoy this meal, let us appreciate the blessings we have received. Everyone has the opportunity to experience true peace and happiness.

translations.source: Mmadụ nile nwere ike ịma ihe. Sọ ohe nọchiri ụzọ bụ ekweghị ekwe nke anyi na ụjọ.
translations.reference: Everyone can achieve enlightenment. The only thing standing in the way of this goal is our own tension and negativity.
translations.hypothesis: Everyone has the ability to learn. The path to knowledge is open to all, regardless of age or background.

translations.source: Buddhism ndị Tibet dabere n’ụmụ nkuzi nke Buddha, mana adọtịkwuru ha site n’aka ụzọ nke ihụnanya mahayana ya na site n’aka ọtụtụ usoro si na Yoga Indịa.
translations.reference: The Tibetan Buddhism is based on the teachings of Buddha, but were extended by the mahayana path of love and by a lot of techniques from Indian Yoga.
translations.hypothesis: Tibetan Buddhism is based on the teachings of the Buddha, but it has been adapted through the lens of Mahayana Buddhism's emphasis on compassion and through various practices from Indian Yoga.

translations.source: Na ntọala, Buddhism Tibet dị ezigbo mfe. Ọ mejupụtara Yoga Kundalini, ntụgharị uche na ụzọ nke ịhụnanya nnabata-ihe niile.
translations.reference: In principle the Tibetan Buddhism is very simple. It consists of Kundalini Yoga, meditation and the path of all-embracing love.
translations.hypothesis: In its essence, Tibetan Buddhism is a practical and accessible philosophy. It incorporates practices such as Kundalini Yoga, mindfulness, and a compassionate approach to all beings.

translations.source: N’iji Yoga Kundalini ike Kundalini (ike mmepe anya) bụ nke etetara site n’ụmụ postchọ yoga, mgbatị ahụ iku ume, ukwe ntụgharị uche na ihe ngosi.
translations.reference: With Kundalini Yoga the Kundalini energy (enlightenment energy) is awakened through yoga postures, breathing exercises, mantras and visualizations.
translations.hypothesis: The Kundalini Yoga technique involves stimulating the Kundalini energy (the energy located at the base of the spine) through specific yoga postures, breathing exercises, and mental focus.

translations.source: Nke bụ isiokwu ntụgharị uche nke ndị Tibet bụ Deyiti Yoga. Site na ichepụta chi dị iche iche, a na ehichapụta ụkpụrụ ike, kpọghee chakra ma kepụta owuweanya nke amamihe.
translations.reference: The center of Tibetan meditation is the Deity Yoga. Through the visualization of various deities the energy channels are cleaned, the chakras are activated and the enlightenment consciousness is created.
translations.hypothesis: This is a summary of the Tibetan Buddhist practice of Deyiti Yoga. Through the visualization of different deities, practitioners cultivate inner strength, open their chakras, and develop a deep sense of compassion and wisdom.

translations.source: Jamini bụ ndị iro ọha n'Agha Ụwa nke abụọ, nke mere mba USA na USSR ji nwee mmekọ. Ka agha gwụrụ, esemokwu usoro omume, na omenala mere mba ndị ahụ ji nwee okwu.
translations.reference: Germany was a common enemy in World War 2, leading to cooperation between the USSR and USA. With the end of the war the clashes of system, process and culture led to the countries falling out.
translations.hypothesis: Jamini was a major cause of World War II, leading to the alliance between the United States and the Soviet Union. After the war, the two countries experienced ideological differences and conflicting interests, which led to a period of tension and rivalry.

translations.source: N'etiti afọ abụọ nke nlụcha nke agha ahụ, ndị mba bụbu ndị mmekọrịta bụzi ndị iro ugbu a ma Agha Oyi ahụ bidokwara.
translations.reference: With two years of the end of the war, the former allies were now enemies and the Cold War began.
translations.hypothesis: During the two-year period of the war, former allies have now become enemies, and the conflict has intensified.

translations.source: O kwesịrị ịnọru ruo afọ iri anọ na-abịa abịa ma a ga-alụkwa ya n'ezie, site n'aka ụsụụ ndị agha nnọchite, n'ama agha site n'Afrịka ruo Eshia, n'ime Afghanistan, Kiuba na ọtụtụ ebe ndị ọzọ.
translations.reference: It was to last for the next 40 years and would be fought for real, by proxy armies, on battlefields from Africa to Asia, in Afghanistan, Cuba and many other places.
translations.hypothesis: It is estimated that over six million people have been displaced due to armed conflict, including refugees from various African countries, as well as internally displaced persons from Afghanistan, Iraq, and other regions.

translations.source: Mgbe Septemba 17, 1939 ruru, a kutuola nchekwa ndị Poland; naanị olileanya ha nwere bụ ịlaghachi tụọ atụmatụ ọzọ n'akụkụ isi briij Romenia.
translations.reference: By September 17, 1939, the Polish defense was already broken, and the only hope was to retreat and reorganise along the Romanian bridgehead.
translations.hypothesis: On September 17, 1939, Poland was invaded; their only option was to retreat and regroup on the other side of the Romanian border.

translations.source: Mana, o gbughi oge ka atụmatụ a niile laa n'efu, mgbe ihe karịrị ndị Sọviet Yunịọn Red Amị 800,000 banyere, kepụta ogige agha ndị Belarụs na Yukren, ka ha wakpochara akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ Poland na nnupu isi nye Nkwekọrịta Udo Riga, Nkwekọrịta Udo Sọviet Yunịọn na Poland, na ọtụtụ nkwekọrịta ndị ọzọ, ma nke dị n'etiti mba abụọ, na nke dị n'etiti ọtụtụ mba.
translations.reference: However, these plans were rendered obsolete nearly overnight, when over 800,000 soldiers from the Soviet's Union Red Army entered and created the Belarussian and Ukrainian fronts after invading the eastern regions of Poland in violation of the Riga Peace Treaty, the Soviet-Polish Non-Aggression Pact, and other international treaties, both bilateral and multilateral.
translations.hypothesis: Therefore, the period of intense military activity, involving over 800,000 Soviet troops, marked the final stages of the war in Eastern Europe, as the Red Army pushed westward through Belarus and Ukraine, capturing key cities such as Riga and Warsaw, and ultimately contributing to the collapse of the Soviet-Polish alliance and numerous other agreements, both between the two countries and between the Soviet Union and other nations.

translations.source: Iji ụgbọ mmiri ebughari ngwa ahịa bụ ụzọ kachasị mma n'ezie iji buru ọtụtụ ndị na ọtụtụ ngwa gafee oke osimiri.
translations.reference: Using ships to transport goods is by far the most efficient way to move large amounts of people and goods across oceans.
translations.hypothesis: The use of a barge is the most effective way to transport a large number of people and goods across a wide river.

translations.source: Ọrụ nke ndị agha nke mmiri abụrụla kemgbe ịgba mbọ hụ na mba gị jidesiri ike ikikere ibugharị ndị gị na ngwaahịa gị, ma n'otu mgbe ahụ, na-egbochi ikikere onye iro gị ibugharị ndị ya na ngwaahịa ya.
translations.reference: The job of navies has traditionally been to ensure that your country maintains the ability to move your people and goods, while at the same time, interfering with your enemy's ability to move his people and goods.
translations.hypothesis: The role of naval forces has evolved over time, from primarily defending a nation's coastline and trade routes from enemy attacks, to also projecting power and influence abroad.

translations.source: Otu n’ime ọmụmatụ oge na-etebeghị anya nke a kacha tozuo oke bụbu kampeenụ Ugwu Atlantik nke WWII. Ndị Amerịka nọ na-anwa ibugharị ụmụ nwoke na ngwongwo gafee Oke osimiri Atlantik inyere Britenụ aka.
translations.reference: One of the most noteworthy recent examples of this was the North Atlantic campaign of WWII. The Americans were trying to move men and materials across the Atlantic Ocean to help Britain.
translations.hypothesis: One of the most significant turning points in World War II was the Battle of the Atlantic. American forces were determined to disrupt German U-boat operations in the Atlantic, which were hindering Britain's ability to receive supplies.

translations.source: N'otu mgbe ahụ, ndị agha nke mmiri nke Jamanị, n'iji naanị ụgbọokpurummiri, nọ na-agbalị ịkwụsị mkpọchi ụzọ a.
translations.reference: At the same time, the German navy, using mainly U-boats, was trying to stop this traffic.
translations.hypothesis: At that time, the Jamanite army, using only boats, were attempting to block the road.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ndị mba bụbu ndị mmekọrịta dara, Jamanị nwere ike eleghi anya merie Briten dị ka o mere Yurop ndị ọzọ fọdụrụ.
translations.reference: Had the Allies failed, Germany probably would have been able to conquer Britain as it had the rest of Europe.
translations.hypothesis: If the Igbo people were to become allies with Britain, then James might have been able to defeat the British as he had done in other European conflicts.

translations.source: Ewu yiri ka e buru ụzọ mee ya anụụlọ n’ihe ruru puku afọ iri gara aga n'ugwu Zagros nke Iran.
translations.reference: Goats seem to have been first domesticated roughly 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of Iran.
translations.hypothesis: The eagle was seen flying over the Zagros Mountains in Iran, a region that has been inhabited for thousands of years.

translations.source: Omenala ndị mgbe ochie na agbụrụ bidoro iji dobe ha maka inweta ohere dị mfe na mmiri ara, ntutu isi, anụ, na anụahụ gasị.
translations.reference: Ancient cultures and tribes began to keep them for easy access to milk, hair, meat, and skins.
translations.hypothesis: Traditional practices in the past and present have been used to obtain resources such as water, food, firewood, and other essential items.

translations.source: E dobere n'ozuzu ụmụ ehu ụlọ n'ime ìgwè ndị nke pagharịrị n'elu ugwu ma ọ bụ ebe ịta ahịhịa ndị ọzọ, nke ọtụtụ mgbe bụ ndị ọzụzụ ehu na-elekọta ha ndị nke na abụkarị ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ụmụ ntorọbịa, nke yiri onye ọzụzụ atụrụ a ka mara ama. A ka na-eji usoro ọzụzụ ehu ndị a ruo taa.
translations.reference: Domestic goats were generally kept in herds that wandered on hills or other grazing areas, often tended by goatherds who were frequently children or adolescents, similar to the more widely known shepherd. These methods of herding are still used today.
translations.hypothesis: The practice of raising young children in separate rooms within a household, often with dedicated caregivers, is a common one. These caregivers are typically mothers or other female relatives, and they provide the children with the care and attention they need. This method of raising children has been used for centuries.

translations.source: E wuru ụzọ ụgbọ ibu gasị n’Ingland dị ka n'oge dị ka narị afọ nke iri na isii ahụ.
translations.reference: Wagonways were built in England as early as the 16th Century.
translations.hypothesis: The first automobile was invented in England during the late 18th century.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị ụmụ ụzọwagọn nwere naanị ogwe osisi nọ n’akụkụ n’akụkụ, ha nyere ụmụ ịnyịnya na-esere ha òhèrè irute ekwomọsọ ndị karịrị ma sere ibu kara dị ukwuu karịa n’ụmụ ụzọ nke ụbọchị ahụ ndị karịtụrụ dị ike ike.
translations.reference: Although wagonways merely consisted of parallel planks of wood, they allowed horses pulling them to achieve greater speeds and pull larger loads than on the slightly more rough roads of the day.
translations.hypothesis: The paths were only covered with grass, providing a smooth and easy surface for the children to walk on, and the ground was much firmer than the uneven terrain of the previous day.

translations.source: Ebidoro mgbe gboo were krọstaị na-arụ ụzọ ụgbọoloko ka o were gbasie ike. Obere obere a bịa mata na ụzọ ụgbọoloko ga-esikarị ike ma ọ bụrụ na o nweturu obere igwe n’elu ya.
translations.reference: Crossties were introduced fairly early to hold the tracks in place. Gradually, however, it was realised that tracks would be more efficient if they had a stip of iron on the top.
translations.hypothesis: The road was initially paved with asphalt, but over time, it began to deteriorate. Small cracks appeared in the pavement, and eventually, the road became impassable without a heavy-duty vehicle.

translations.source: Nke mechara bụrụ omume a na-emekarị, mana igwe ahụ kpatakwuru ndọwa n'ụkwụ ụmụ ụgbọ ibu ejiri osisi mee.
translations.reference: This became common practice, but the iron caused more wear on the wooden wheels of the wagons.
translations.hypothesis: This was a common practice in the past, but the use of wooden wheels made of reeds has become obsolete.

translations.source: N'ikpeazụ, eji wiil ígwè dochie wiil osisi. N'afọ 1767, e wepụtara wiil nke mbụ ejị igwe rụọ kpam kpam.
translations.reference: Eventually, wooden wheels were replaced by iron wheels. In 1767, the first full-iron rails were introduced.
translations.hypothesis: First, let's talk about the history of paper. In 1767, the first paper mill was established.

translations.source: Usoro njem e bu ụzọ mara ama bụ ịga ije, ụmụ mmadụ bidoro ịkwụ ọtọ aga ije afọ nde abụọ gara aga site na mpụta nke Homo Erektus (nke pụtara nwoke kwụ ọtọ).
translations.reference: The first known transportation was walking, humans began walking upright two million years ago with the emergence of Homo Erectus (meaning upright man).
translations.hypothesis: The earliest known form of bipedalism was walking, with humans spending approximately two million years walking on two legs.

translations.source: Ndị bụ ha ụzọ, Ọstralopitekus ahụ akwụghị ọtọ gaa ije dị ka n'akparamagwa.
translations.reference: Their predecessors, the Australopithecus did not walk upright as habitually.
translations.hypothesis: They were upright, the Australopithecus walked upright like modern humans.

translations.source: Achoputara ọkachamara bipedal na fosil Australopithecus site na nde nde afọ 4.2-3.9 gara aga, o bu ezie na Sahelanthropus nwere ike ije ije n'ukwu abuo na nde afọ asaa gara aga.
translations.reference: Bipedal specializations are found in Australopithecus fossils from 4.2-3.9 million years ago, although Sahelanthropus may have walked on two legs as early as seven million years ago.
translations.hypothesis: The discovery of the bipedal fossil of Australopithecus, dating back to between 4.2 and 3.9 million years ago, provides further evidence that Sahelanthropus may have also walked upright around 6 million years ago.

translations.source: Anyị nwere ike malite ibi n’enyi karịa na gburugburu ebe obibi, anyị nwere ike isonye ije nke gburugburu ebe obibi, ma anyị nwekwara ike ịbụ ndị ọchọ mgbanwe ka e nwee ike belata ntaramahụhụ ọdịnihu ruo ogo ụfọdụ.
translations.reference: We can start living more friendly to the environment, we can join to the environmental movement, and we can even be activists in order to reduce the future suffering in some degree.
translations.hypothesis: We can start by educating ourselves and others about the importance of protecting our environment, and we can also take action to reduce our own environmental impact.

translations.source: Nke a dị nnọọ ka ọgwụgwọ kemgbaàmà n’ọtụtụ okwu. Agbanyeghị, ọ bụrụ na anyị achọghị naanị ọsịsa nke nwa oge, ya mere anyị kwesịrị ịchọta isi ihe kpatara nsogbu ndị ahụ, ma anyị kwesịrị iwepụ̀ ike ha.
translations.reference: This is just like symptomatic treatment in many cases. However, if we do not only want a temporary solution, then we should find the root of the problems, and we should deactivate them.
translations.hypothesis: This is essentially a treatment for a common ailment. However, if we only focus on suppressing the symptoms, we need to identify the underlying cause and address it directly.

translations.source: O doro anya nke ọma n'ụwa agbanweela nnukwu n'ihi ụmụ ọganihu nke sayensị na teknụzụ nke ụmụ mmadụ, ma ụmụ nsogbu adịla nnukwu karịa n'ihi ọnụọgụgụ mmadụ karịrị akarị na ibifụga ndụ ókè nke ụmụ mmadụ.
translations.reference: It is obvious enough that the world has changed much because of humankind's scientific and technological advancements, and problems have become greater because of overpopulation and mankind's extravagant lifestyle.
translations.hypothesis: The world has undergone significant changes due to the advancements in science and technology, but new problems have also emerged, such as overpopulation and the increasing rate of human-caused environmental degradation.

translations.source: Mgbe Kọngres nyechara ya nkwekọrịta ha na Julaị 4, e weere ya n'akwụkwọ eji aka dee, nke Jọn Hankọk Onye isi Kọngres na Chals Tọmsin Onye odeakwụkwọ tinyere akara nkwado ha, wega ya n'ụlọ mbipụta Jọn Dunlap nke eteghi aka.
translations.reference: After its adoption by Congress on July 4, a handwritten draft signed by the President of Congress John Hancock and the Secretary Charles Thomson was then sent a few blocks away to the printing shop of John Dunlap.
translations.hypothesis: After the Congress passed the agreement on July 4, it was printed in a formal document, signed by John Hancock, the President of the Congress, and Charles Thomson, the Secretary. A copy was also presented to John Dunlap, the printer.

translations.source: N'ime abali n'etiti mbipụta otu narị na iri ise ya na narị abụọ ka e mere, nke a mara ugbu a dị ka “Dunlap broadsides”.
translations.reference: Through the night between 150 and 200 copies were made, now known as "Dunlap broadsides".
translations.hypothesis: During the period between the late 18th and early 19th centuries, a type of printed material known today as "Dunlap broadsides" was produced.

translations.source: Oge mbụ a gụpụtara edemede a n'ọha bụ na Julaị 8, nke John Nixn gụrụ na mbaraezi Ụlọọgbakọ Ndipenda.
translations.reference: The first public reading of the document was by John Nixon in the yard of Independence Hall on July 8.
translations.hypothesis: The first time this document was published was on July 8, when John Nixon found it in the archives of the First Presbyterian Church.

translations.source: Na Julaị 6, e zigaara George Washington otu kọpị, onye mere ka a gụọrọ ya ndị agha ya na Niu Yọk na Julaị 9. Otu kọpị ruru Lọndọn n'Ọgọstụ 10.
translations.reference: One was sent to George Washington on July 6, who had it read to his troops in New York on July 9. A copy reached London on August 10.
translations.hypothesis: On July 6, George Washington issued a proclamation calling for troops to assemble in New York on July 9. A second proclamation was issued on August 10, calling for troops to assemble in Philadelphia.

translations.source: Dunlap brọdsaịd 25 ka nọ taa bụ kọpị edemede izizi ndị kachasị dị ochie. Nke izizi e ji aka dee anọzighi.
translations.reference: The 25 Dunlap broadsides still known to exist are the oldest surviving copies of the document. The original handwritten copy has not survived.
translations.hypothesis: The Dunlap Broadside No. 25 is one of the oldest surviving printed broadsides. It features an image of a man using his hand to point.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ndị ọkàchamara ihe banyere fọsịl anụmanụ na osisi taa kwenyere na otu òtù daịnosọọ lanarịrị ma dị ndụ taa. Anyị na-akpọ ha ụmụ nnụnụ.
translations.reference: Many paleontologists today believe that one group of dinosaurs survived and is alive today. We call them birds.
translations.hypothesis: Several scientists have concluded that the fossil record shows a clear progression from primitive forms of animals and plants to the diverse and complex forms we see today. They refer to these early forms as ancestors.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ anaghị eche bayere ha dị ka daịnosọọ n'ihi na ha nwere nku ma nwee ike ife efe.
translations.reference: Many people don't think about them as dinosaurs because they have feathers and can fly.
translations.hypothesis: Many people are unable to recognize themselves in the mirror because they have scars or other physical imperfections.

translations.source: Mana a ka nwere ọtụtụ ihe gbasara ụmụ nnụnụ ndị yiri nke daịnosọọ.
translations.reference: But there are a lot of things about birds that still look like a dinosaur.
translations.hypothesis: There are many different types of baby food available.

translations.source: Ha nwere okpa ya na abuba na mbu aka, ha na eyi akwa, ha nakwa aga ije na ukwu oji ha abuo dika T-Rex.
translations.reference: They have feet with scales and claws, they lay eggs, and they walk on their two back legs like a T-Rex.
translations.hypothesis: They had large, powerful legs, and their bodies were long and slender, resembling those of a T-Rex.

translations.source: Ihe dịka igwe kọmputa niile e ji arụ ọrụ taa bụ ihe sitere na mkpụrụokwu ndị a gwakọrọ agwakọ nke e tinyere dịka mkpụrụọnụọgụ.
translations.reference: Virtually all computers in use today are based on the manipulation of information which is coded in the form of binary numbers.
translations.hypothesis: The modern computer, as we know it today, is based on the principles outlined in these fundamental concepts, such as binary code.

translations.source: Otu akara ọnụọgụ abụọ nwere ike inwe naanị otu n’ime mbamuru abụọ, ya bụ 0 ma ọ bụ 1, ma a na-akpọ akara ndị a dị ka ọnụọgụ keọnụọgụ abụọ - ma ọ bụ bits, iji asụsụ mpụiche kọmputa.
translations.reference: A binary number can have only one of two values, i.e. 0 or 1, and these numbers are referred to as binary digits - or bits, to use computer jargon.
translations.hypothesis: A binary digit can only have one of two values, either 0 or 1, and these digits are referred to as binary digits, or bits, in computer language.

translations.source: Ọrịa ịtụ nsị nke ime ahụ nwere ike ọ gaghị adị ire ozigbo. Ihe ngosipụta ya, dịka ọgbụgbọ, bụ ihe ndị na-emekwa n'ọtụtụ ọrịa ndị ọzọ. Ya mere na enweghi ike ịchọpụta ọrịa a ozigbo ozigbo.
translations.reference: Internal poisoning may not be immediately apparent. Symptoms, such as vomiting are sufficiently general that an immediate diagnosis cannot be made.
translations.hypothesis: The symptom of a swollen abdomen may not always be present. However, other symptoms, such as abdominal pain, can also be present in other diseases. Therefore, it is not possible to definitively diagnose this condition based on these symptoms alone.

translations.source: Ndosipụta kachasị mma maka inwe ńsí n’ime ahụ nwere ike ịbụ ọnụnọ nke mkpọ ogwụ ghe oghe ma ọ bụ kemikalụ ezinụlọ ndị na-egbu agbu.
translations.reference: The best indication of internal poisoning may be the presence of an open container of medication or toxic household chemicals.
translations.hypothesis: The best way to get rid of mold in a room is to eliminate the source of moisture, such as a leaky pipe or chemical substances that promote its growth.

translations.source: Lelee nnyeàhà ahụ maka ntụziaka mgbata ọsọ enyemaka mbụ akọwapụtara maka nsi ahụ akọwapụtara.
translations.reference: Check the label for specific first aid instructions for that specific poison.
translations.hypothesis: Please refer to the first aid instructions I provided for guidance on how to handle the injury.

translations.source: okwu bụ ahụhụ bụ ndị ọka mmụta ahụhụ n’ụzọ nwere ugwu maka òtù ụmụ ahụhụ a.
translations.reference: The term bug is used by entomologists in a formal sense for this group of insects.
translations.hypothesis: The books are educational materials designed to be engaging and informative for young readers.

translations.source: Okwu a sitere mmarita mgbe-ochie nke akpiri, bu chinchi di oke nko maka ibunye ndi mmadu oria.
translations.reference: This term derives from ancient familiarity with Bed-bugs, which are insects highly adapted to parasitize humans.
translations.hypothesis: This refers to the concept of marriage, which is a formal union between two people.

translations.source: Ma Assassin-bọg na Bed-bọg dị nidikolous, ha zuru oke ibi na nest maọbụ n'ụlọ nke hostu ha.
translations.reference: Both Assassin-bugs and Bed-bugs are nidicolous, adapted to living in nest or housing of their host.
translations.hypothesis: The Assassin-birds and Bed-birds typically build their nests in trees or on the roofs of buildings.

translations.source: N'ofe mba Amerịka, e nwere ihe dị ka ọnụọgụ ọrịa Multiple Sclerosis (MS) 400,000 a maara amaara, nke na-eme ya isi ọrịa ụbụrụ na-emetụta ndị ntorọbịa na ndị okenye.
translations.reference: Across the United States of America, there are approximately 400,000 known cases of Multiple Sclerosis (MS), leaving it as the leading neurological disease in younger and middle aged adults.
translations.hypothesis: In the United States, there are an estimated 400,000 people who are unaware they have Multiple Sclerosis (MS), a chronic autoimmune disease that affects the brain and spinal cord.

translations.source: Mọltipụl Sklerosis bụ ọrịa na-emetụta sentral navọs sistem, nke gbakwunyere ụbụrụ, ogwurugwu azụ na ọptik nav.
translations.reference: MS is a disease that affects the central nervous system, which is made up of the brain, the spinal cord and the optic nerve.
translations.hypothesis: Multiple sclerosis is a disease that affects the central nervous system, including the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves.

translations.source: Nnyocha achọpụtala na ụmụ nwanyị bụ ihe yikarịrị ugboro abụọ inwe MS karịa ụmụ nwoke.
translations.reference: Research has found that females are two times more likely to have MS then males.
translations.hypothesis: Research has shown that women are twice as likely to develop multiple sclerosis (MS) as men.

translations.source: Di na nwunye nwere ike ikwekọrịta na ọ gaghị abara ha maọbụ nwa ha uru ịzụpụta nwa.
translations.reference: A couple may decide it is not in their best interest, or in the interest of their child, to raise a baby.
translations.hypothesis: The wife may be unable to conceive, or she may have experienced a miscarriage or stillbirth.

translations.source: Di na nwunye ndị a nwere ike ịhọrọ ime atụmatụ mkpọta nwa maka nwa ha.
translations.reference: These couples may choose to make an adoption plan for their baby.
translations.hypothesis: These mothers may choose to have a joint adoption of a child.

translations.source: N’ime otu mkpọRọ nwa, nne na nna mụrụ nwa ahụ ga-akwụsị ikikere ha dị ka nne na nna ka di na nwunye ọ bụla nwere ike izulite nwa ahụ.
translations.reference: In an adoption, the birth parents terminate their parental rights so that another couple may parent the child.
translations.hypothesis: In a family, the parents will always be the primary caregivers for their child, and they will be the ones who make decisions about the child's upbringing.

translations.source: Isi ọrụ sayensị bụ ịchọpụta otu ụwa si arụ ọrụ site na usoro kesayensị. Usoro n'ezie na-edu ọtụtụ n'ime nnyocha kesayensị.
translations.reference: Science’s main goal is to figure out the way the world works through the scientific method. This method in fact guides most scientific research.
translations.hypothesis: The purpose of scientific research is to discover new knowledge through the application of scientific methods. These methods involve a variety of techniques and procedures.

translations.source: Ọ nọghị naanị ya n'ezie, eksperimenteshọn, ma otu eksperimenti bụ otu ule nke eji ewepụ otu haịpotesis kwere omume ma ọ bụ karịa, ịjụ ajụjụ gasị, na ime nyochata nakwa eduzi nnyocha sayensị.
translations.reference: It isn’t alone though, experimentation, and an experiment is a test that is used to eliminate one or more of the possible hypotheses, asking questions, and making observations also guide scientific research.
translations.hypothesis: It is not just a simple experiment, but a systematic process. Each experiment is a test of a hypothesis, involving careful questioning, observation, and data collection to support or refute a scientific theory.

translations.source: Ndị ọkammụta n'ụmụ ihe ekere na ndị ọkachamara gbadoro ụkwụ n'ederede oge gboo, ọkachasị, n'akwụkwọ nsọ e dere na Latin.
translations.reference: Naturalists and philosophers focused on classical texts and, in particular, on the Bible in Latin.
translations.hypothesis: The educational materials and experts involved in the project have been working diligently, particularly in the preparation of documents written in Latin.

translations.source: A nabatara echiche Aristotle gbasara okwu sayensi niile ma mmuta akparamagwa ya bu psychology
translations.reference: Accepted were Aristotle's views on all matters of science, including psychology.
translations.hypothesis: Aristotle, a renowned philosopher, laid the foundation for the scientific study of psychology.

translations.source: Dika amamihe nke ndi Greek biara gbatuwa, ndi odida anyanwu huta onwe ha ka ha na egbubiri site mgbara-ogwu ndi Greek ha nke ihe-omuma na nka.
translations.reference: As knowledge of Greek declined, the West found itself cut off from its Greek philosophical and scientific roots.
translations.hypothesis: Similar to the ancient Greeks, the Western civilization developed its own unique artistic and philosophical traditions, drawing inspiration from Greek thought and culture.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ usoro a na-ahụ na fisiọlọji na omume na-adabere ọtụtụ mgbe n'usoro ime ahụ na mmepụta ha site n'elekere nke ime ahụ.
translations.reference: Many observed rhythms in physiology and behavior often crucially depend on the presence of endogenous cycles and their production through biological clocks.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the processes observed in physiology and psychology are frequently seen in the human body and its functions, from the moment of birth to death.

translations.source: Usoro kwa-oge kwa-oge, nke n'abụghị nzaghachi nye ntụpenye kwa-oge keezi, ka edeturula maka ọtụtụ ihe ndị dị ndụ , nke gụnyere nje bakterịa, fọngaị, akụmakụ na ụmụanụmanụ.
translations.reference: Periodic rhythms, which are not simply responses to external periodic cues, have been documented for most living beings, including bacteria, fungi, plants, and animals.
translations.hypothesis: This type of soil, which is not suitable for most plants, is rich in minerals and can support the growth of bacteria, fungi, and other microorganisms.

translations.source: Elekere ime ahụ nwere usoro eje alọ nke na-arụ ọrụ n'onwe ya; usoro a ga na-aga n'ihu ma asịgodị rịị na onweghi ihe ọzọ metụtara ya.
translations.reference: Biological clocks are self sustaining oscillators which will continue a period of free-running cycling even in the absence of external cues.
translations.hypothesis: The structure of the building has a self-supporting design; this means that it can stand on its own without any external support.

translations.source: Nwale Hershey na Chase so na otu aro no na isi siri na DNA wubu otu mkpụrụ ndụ ihe nketa.
translations.reference: The Hershey and Chase experiment was one of the leading suggestions that DNA was a genetic material.
translations.hypothesis: Nuclease Hershey and Chase used a radioactive tracer to demonstrate that DNA is the genetic material of living cells.

translations.source: Hershey na Chase jiri ụmụ feeji, ma ọ bụ ụmụ nje, iji kụnye DNA nke ha n'ime otu nje bakterịọm.
translations.reference: Hershey and Chase used phages, or viruses, to implant their own DNA into a bacterium.
translations.hypothesis: Hershey and Chase used bacteriophages, or viruses, to package the DNA of bacteria into a single virus particle.

translations.source: Ha mere nnwale abụọ ebe ha ji rediyoaktiv fosforọs kaa akara na DNA nọ na fej maọbụ jiri rediyoaktiv sọlfọ kaa akara na protin nọ na fej.
translations.reference: They did two experiments marking either the DNA in the phage with a radioactive phosphorus or the protein of the phage with radioactive sulfur.
translations.hypothesis: They used two different methods: one involved using radioactive phosphorus to label DNA, and the other involved using radioactive sulfur to label proteins.

translations.source: Mgbanwe ọjọọ nwere ike inwe ọtụtụ mmetụta dị iche iche na ndabere na ụdị mgbanwe ọjọọ ọ bụ, abamuru nke otu iberibe nke ihe mkpụrụ ndụ ihe nketa o metụtara na ma ọ bụrụ na ụmụ mkpụrụ ndụ o metụtara bụ ụmụ mkpụrụ ndụ geem-laịnụ.
translations.reference: Mutations can have a variety of different effects depending on the type of mutation, the significance of the piece of genetic material affected and whether the cells affected are germ-line cells.
translations.hypothesis: Changes in temperature can have various effects depending on the type of change and the organisms affected. For example, a sudden drop in temperature can cause frost damage to plants, while a gradual increase in temperature can help plants to grow and reproduce.

translations.source: Ọ bụ nanị mgbanwe na mkpụrụ ndụ jem-laịn ka a ga-enyefe ụmụaka, ebe mgbanwe n’ebe ndị ọzọ nwere ike ibute ọnwụ nke mkpụrụ ndụ maọbụ ọrịa kansa.
translations.reference: Only mutations in germ-line cells can be passed on to children, while mutations elsewhere can cause cell-death or cancer.
translations.hypothesis: The only known cause of this condition is a genetic mutation, while changes in other areas may lead to the death of cells or cancer.

translations.source: Njem-nlere anya nke dabere na udidi na enweta uche ndi mmadu ndi nwere mmasi izute ebe di na udidi ha maka ihi ikpori-ndu na udi ebe, gunyekwara akumaku anumanu anu-ohia.
translations.reference: Nature-based tourism attracts people interested in visiting natural areas for the purpose of enjoying the scenery, including plant and animal wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: The research focused on identifying and analyzing the factors that contribute to the high rates of infant mortality in a specific community, with the aim of developing effective interventions to reduce the number of deaths.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ ihe omume enwere ike ime ma anọrọ ya gụnyere ịchụ nta, ịkụ azụ, ise foto, ilele nnụnụ, na ịga n'ogige gụọ maka ihe ndị dị ndụ na gburugburu ha.
translations.reference: Examples of on-site activities include hunting, fishing, photography, bird watching, and visiting parks and studying information about the ecosystem.
translations.hypothesis: Some activities that can be done while respecting the environment include hiking, birdwatching, taking photographs, visiting nature reserves, and reading about the local flora and fauna.

translations.source: Otu ọmụmaatụ bụ ileta, ise fòto, na ịmụta gbasara na ụmụ ọrangụtanụ nọ n'ime Bọnioo.
translations.reference: An example is visiting, photographing, and learning about organgatuangs in Borneo.
translations.hypothesis: The workshop involved lectures, presentations, and hands-on activities focused on the diverse range of species found in the Bono region.

translations.source: Ututu o bula, ndi mmadu n'ahapu obere obodo n'ugbo ala were gawa ulo oru ha ma ndi ozo n'agbafe ha ndi ulo oru ha di n'ebe ha si puta.
translations.reference: Every morning, people leave small country towns in cars to go their workplace and are passed by others whose work destination is the place they have just left.
translations.hypothesis: The village was in a state of chaos, with people running in all directions as the floodwaters rose. The villagers were desperate to save their homes and belongings, but the rising water made it impossible.

translations.source: N'ime ụgbọ mgbagharị kenjem a na-agbanwegharị agbanwe onye ọ bụla si n'otuọdịla metụta ya, ma na-akwado, otu sistemụ njem dabere na ụgbọala nkeonwe.
translations.reference: In this dynamic transport shuttle everyone is somehow connected with, and supporting, a transport system based on private cars.
translations.hypothesis: In this evolving transportation system, each individual chooses a mode of transport that best suits their needs, while still contributing to a cohesive overall system.

translations.source: Sayensị na-egosi ugbu a na ekọnọmi a ji oke kabọn arụ ọrụ akupụla mkpokọta ihe ndụ niile nọ n'ụwa site n'otu n'ime ọnọdụ nkwụsi ike ya nke kwadogoro obibi ndụ mmadụ n'afọ nde abụọ gara aga.
translations.reference: Science now indicates that this massive carbon economy has dislodged the biosphere from one of its stable states that has supported human evolution for the past two million years.
translations.hypothesis: The latest statistics reveal a significant increase in global unemployment rates, with millions of people losing their jobs in the past two years due to the economic downturn.

translations.source: Onye ọ bụla na-esonye n'ime ọha mmadụ ma na-eji ụmụ sistemụ njem. Ọ fọrọ obere ka ọ bụrụ onye niile na eme mkpesa gbasara ụmụ sistemụ njem.
translations.reference: Everyone participates in society and uses transportation systems. Almost everyone complains about transportation systems.
translations.hypothesis: Anyone who participates in the global community and uses transportation systems. It is becoming increasingly clear that everyone is concerned about the impact of transportation systems.

translations.source: N'ime ụmụ mba mepere emepe ọ ga-ara ahụ tupu ị nụ larịị mkpesa ndị yirinụ gbasara ogo mmiri ma ọ bụ ụmụ akwa mmiri na-ada n'ala.
translations.reference: In developed countries you seldom hear similar levels of complaints about water quality or bridges falling down.
translations.hypothesis: In the meantime, we will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates on the water levels and any potential flooding risks.

translations.source: Gịnị mere sistemụ njem ji akpata ụdịrị ụmụ mkpesa ahụ, gịmị mere ha ji ada kwa ụbọchị? Ọ bụ na ndị injinịa njem amaghị arụ ọrụ ha nke ọma? Ma ọ bụ ihe ọzọ si n'isi na-eme?
translations.reference: Why do transportation systems engender such complaints, why do they fail on a daily basis? Are transportation engineers just incompetent? Or is something more fundamental going on?
translations.hypothesis: What caused the system to malfunction, and why did it fail to operate correctly every day? Were the engineers responsible for maintaining the system negligent in their duties? Or was there some other underlying issue?

translations.source: Ọwụwụ trafik bụ ọmụmụ nke ngagharị nke onye ọkwụ ụgbọ ọ bụla na ụgbọ ha n'etiti akara abụọ na mmekọrịta ha na-eme n'etiti onwe ha.
translations.reference: Traffic Flow is the study of the movement of individual drivers and vehicles between two points and the interactions they make with one another.
translations.hypothesis: Website traffic refers to the number of visits a website receives from individual users or through their devices, as they interact with the website and its content.

translations.source: Na mwute, ịmụ maka otu okporo njem si aga siri maka na e nweghi ike ikwu kpọm n'ọgụ otu narị pasentị ụdị omume ọkwọ ụgbọ nwere ike ime.
translations.reference: Unfortunately, studying traffic flow is difficult because driver behavior cannot be predicted with one-hundred percent certainty.
translations.hypothesis: In short, the study found that a specific type of vehicle, a motorcycle, was involved in a significant number of accidents, with a rate of 10% higher than the average for all types of vehicles.

translations.source: Ọ dabara nke ọma na ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala nwere usoro omume na-adịgide; ya mere, ụzọ njem moto anaghị agbanwecha agbanwe ma bụrụkwa ihe enwere ike iji eserese aritmetik gosipụta.
translations.reference: Fortunately, drivers tend to behave within a reasonably consistent range; thus, traffic streams tend to have some reasonable consistency and can be roughly represented mathematically.
translations.hypothesis: It is important to note that the methods of transportation used by people have remained relatively consistent over time. Therefore, the principles of motion and mechanics can be used to explain how vehicles work.

translations.source: Iji ka mma na-anọchi anya ije nke okporo ụzọ, E mebewo mmekọrịta n'etiti isi njirimara atọ ahụ: (1) eruba, (2) njupụta, na (3) ike ọsọ.
translations.reference: To better represent traffic flow, relationships have been established between the three main characteristics: (1) flow, (2) density, and (3) velocity.
translations.hypothesis: As the road progresses, I observe the interaction between three key elements: (1) friction, (2) deformation, and (3) speed.

translations.source: Mmetụta ndị a na-enyere aka n’ime atụmatụ, ncheremee, na arụmọrụ nke akụrụngwa okporo ụzọ ụgbọ ígwè.
translations.reference: These relationships help in planning, design, and operations of roadway facilities.
translations.hypothesis: These factors contribute to the efficiency, reliability, and performance of aircraft.

translations.source: Ụmụ ahụhụ bụ ụmụ anụmanụ buru ụzọ fee n'elu. Ike ha n'ife efe nyere ha aka ịgbanaha ndị iro n'ụzọ kara dị mfe ma ịchọtakwa nri na ndị otu mmekọ n'ụzọ dị werewere.
translations.reference: Insects were the first animals to take to the air. Their ability to fly helped them evade enemies more easily and find food and mates more efficiently.
translations.hypothesis: These birds are known for their ability to fly. Their wings allow them to soar through the air, and they use their beaks to feed on insects and other small creatures.

translations.source: Ihe karịrị ọtụtụ n’ime ụmụ ahụhụ nwere uru nke inwe ike ịpịa nku ha gaa n’ahụ ha.
translations.reference: Most insects have the advantage of being able to fold their wings back along the body.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the buttons on a remote control are designed to be easily pressed.

translations.source: Nke a na-eme ka ha nwee ọtụtụ ebe izonarị ndị na-eri ha.
translations.reference: This gives them a wider range of small places to hide from predators.
translations.hypothesis: This suggests that they have a variety of places where they can obtain food.

translations.source: Ubochi taa, nani ogugu nwere ike ikpalaga nku ya azu bu ogugu drago na ogugu may.
translations.reference: Today, the only insects that cannot fold back their wings are dragon flies and mayflies.
translations.hypothesis: The question is, how can we prevent the spread of this type of infectious disease, which can affect both adults and children?

translations.source: Ọtụtụ puku afọ gara aga, otu nwoke a kpọrọ Aristarchus kwuru si na Usoro Mbara Igwe nọ na-agagharị gburugburu Anyanwụ.
translations.reference: Thousands of years ago, a man called Aristarchus said that the Solar System moved around the Sun.
translations.hypothesis: Many centuries ago, a man named Aristarchus proposed that the Earth revolves around the Sun.

translations.source: Ufodu ndi mmadu chere na ihe o na-ekwu bu eziokwu mana ufodu ekweghi; na mbara igwe na-agba uwa okirikiri ma anyanwu(ma kwa kpakpando ndi ozo)
translations.reference: Some people thought he was right but many people believed the opposite; that the Solar System moved around the Earth, including the Sun (and even the other stars).
translations.hypothesis: People believe that what they say is true, but they are often mistaken; the sun rises in the east and sets in the west (a fact known to everyone).

translations.source: Nke a yiri ezi uche, n’ihi na ọ naghị emetụta ka ụwa ọ na-agagharị agagharị, ọ na-emetụta?
translations.reference: This seems sensible, because the Earth doesn't feel as if it's moving, does it?
translations.hypothesis: This is a clever observation, as it highlights the fact that the object does not move on its own, but rather relies on external forces to propel it forward.

translations.source: Osimiri Amazọn ahụ bụ nke abụọ kachasị ogologo na osimiri kachasị n’ibu n’ụwa. Ọ na-ebu ihe karịrị nha mmiri ugboro asatọ dị ka osimiri nke abụọ kachasị ibu.
translations.reference: The Amazon River is the second longest and the biggest river on Earth. It carries more than 8 times as much water as the second biggest river.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon River is the second longest river in the world and the largest by volume. It carries more water than any other river.

translations.source: Amazọn bụkwa osimiri kachasị saa mbara n'ụwa, mgbe ụfọdụ ọ na-eru maịlụ isii.
translations.reference: The Amazon is also the widest river on Earth, at times six miles wide.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon is also the longest river in the world, and it sometimes floods.

translations.source: Pasentị mmmiri 20 zuru oke nke na-awụpụta site na osimiri ụwa ga na-abanye n'ime oke osimiri ga si n'Amazọn abịa.
translations.reference: A full 20 percent of the water that pours out of the planet's rivers into the oceans comes from the Amazon.
translations.hypothesis: The 20 rivers that flow from the Congo River basin into the Atlantic Ocean will eventually flow into the Amazon River.

translations.source: Isi osimiri Amazọnụ dị km 6,387 (maịlị 3,980). Ọ na-ewetaju mmiri site n’ọtụtụ puku osimiri ndị kara di obere.
translations.reference: The main Amazon River is 6,387 km (3,980 miles). It collects water from thousands of smaller rivers.
translations.hypothesis: The Amazon River is approximately 6,387 miles (10,280 kilometers) long. It receives water from numerous tributaries, many of which are quite small.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị na ọrụrụ-piramidi n’okwute gara n’ihu ruo na njedebe nke Alaeze Ochie, ụmụ piramidi nke Giza bụ ndị agafeghị ma ọlị na nha ha na ima mma nka na ụzụ nke ọrụrụ ha.
translations.reference: Although pyramid-building in stone continued until the end of the Old Kingdom, the pyramids of Giza were never surpassed in their size and the technical excellence of their construction.
translations.hypothesis: The pyramids of Giza, a magnificent structure that stood for centuries, have become a symbol of ancient Egyptian civilization and its remarkable achievements in architecture and engineering.

translations.source: O juru ndị Niu Kịngdọm Ijipt mgbe ochie anya ihe ncheta ndị bu ha ụzọ, nke gaferela otu puku afọ mgbe ahụ.
translations.reference: New Kingdom ancient Egyptians marvelled at their predecessors monuments, which were then well over a thousand year old.
translations.hypothesis: The ancient pyramids of Egypt, built thousands of years ago, have stood the test of time.

translations.source: Onu ogugu ndi mmadu obodo Vatican di nari 800. O bu obodo kacha nta n’uwa n’uwa n’uwa na obodo n’ogbe ndi kacha pere mpe.
translations.reference: Vatican City's population is around 800. It is the smallest independent country in the world and the country with the lowest population.
translations.hypothesis: The population of the Vatican City State is approximately 800. It is the smallest country in the world by both area and population.

translations.source: Obodo Vatican na-eji asụsụ Italian na iwu na ukara nkwukọrịta ya.
translations.reference: Vatican City uses Italian in its legislation and official communications.
translations.hypothesis: The Vatican City uses the Italian language and legal system in its internal communications.

translations.source: Asụsụ Itali ka ọtụtụ ndị na-arụ ọrụ na steeti na-asụkwa kwa ụbọchị ebe a na-asụkarị Latin n’emume ndị ụka ga.
translations.reference: Italian is also the everyday language used by most of those who work in the state while Latin is often used in religious ceremonies.
translations.hypothesis: The Italian language is spoken by many people in the state, and it is also used in daily life, particularly in formal settings.

translations.source: Ndị obodo niile nke Obodo Vatican bụ Roman Katọlik.
translations.reference: All citizens of Vatican City are Roman Catholic.
translations.hypothesis: All the inhabitants of the Vatican City are Roman Catholics.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ amarala maka isi kemịkalụ njìmebe ndị dị ka ọlaedo, ọlaọcha, ọla kọpa sitere na oge ochie, dị ka enwere ike ịchọpụta ihe ndị a n’ụwa n’ụdị mbupụtaụwa ma dịrị mfe igwupụta n’iji ngwaọrụ ndị mgbe ochie.
translations.reference: People have known about basic chemical elements such as gold, silver, and copper from antiquity, as these can all be discovered in nature in native form and are relatively simple to mine with primitive tools.
translations.hypothesis: People have long been fascinated by chemical processes such as combustion, oxidation, and fermentation, which have been observed in nature since ancient times. These processes can be studied and understood using simple tools and techniques, making them accessible to anyone interested in learning about them.

translations.source: Aristotle, bụ onye ọka ihe ọmụma, ekwuola na tiori na ihe niile bụ mgwọkọta njimebe otu ma ọ bụ karịa mejupụtara ya. Ha wụbụ aja, mmiri, ikuku, na ọkụ.
translations.reference: Aristotle, a philosopher, theorised that everything is made up of a mixture of one or more of four elements. They were earth, water, air, and fire.
translations.hypothesis: Aristotle, a renowned philosopher, argued that all matter is composed of a finite number of elements, which combine in various proportions. These elements include earth, water, air, and fire.

translations.source: Nke a dị kara yiri ọnọdụ anọ nke mata (n’usoro ahụ kwa): nsiriike, mmiri mmiri, ikuku, na plasma, agbanyeghị na o nyere tiori na ha na-agbanwe ghụọ umi ọhụrụ iji mepụta ihe anyị na-ahụ anya.
translations.reference: This was more like the four states of matter (in the same order): solid, liquid, gas, and plasma, though he also theorised that they change into new substances to form what we see.
translations.hypothesis: The process involves four main stages (repeated in sequence): solid, liquid, gas, and plasma, each of which contributes to the formation of new particles that we perceive as matter.

translations.source: Ụmụ alọị bụgodu mwurikọta ígwè abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa. Echefula na e nwere ọtụtụ njìmebe nọ na tebụlụ pirịọdik.
translations.reference: Alloys are basically a mixture of two or more metals. Don't forget that there are many elements on the periodic table.
translations.hypothesis: The frame of a table typically consists of two or more legs. There are also various other components, such as a tabletop and legs.

translations.source: Ihe ndị dị ka kalsium na potassium bụ igwe. Ee, enwekwara igwe ndị ọzọ dịka ọla ọcha na ọla edo.
translations.reference: Elements like calcium and potassium are considered metals. Of course, there are also metals like silver and gold.
translations.hypothesis: Elements like calcium and potassium are minerals. Yes, there are other minerals such as sodium and chloride.

translations.source: I nwekwara ike nwee allọyi nke gụnyere nwa-obere njieme gasị nke enweghị metalik dịka cabọn.
translations.reference: You can also have alloys that include small amounts of non-metallic elements like carbon.
translations.hypothesis: I have the ability to create a small, non-metallic object, such as a piece of clay.

translations.source: Ihe niile dị na elu ụwa a nwere mata. Mata niile bụ njikọ ọtụtụ obere ihe a na-akpọ atọm.
translations.reference: Everything in the Universe is made of matter. All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms.
translations.hypothesis: Everything in the universe is made up of these tiny particles. All matter is composed of many smaller things called atoms.

translations.source: Atọm pere nnọọ mpe ruo na puku ijeri ga-abali n'ime akara kpọm nọ na ngwụcha okwu a.
translations.reference: Atoms are so incredibly tiny that trillions of them could fit into the period at the end of this sentence.
translations.hypothesis: The number of words in this sentence is approximately one hundred and fifty.

translations.source: Ya mere, pensụl ahụ wụbụ ezigbo enyị nye ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ mgbe ọ pụtara.
translations.reference: Thus, the pencil was a good friend to many people when it came out.
translations.hypothesis: Therefore, the pen has been a valuable tool for many people throughout history.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ihe mwute na ka ụzọ ọhụrụ e si ede ihe na-apụta, 'ọkwa', mkpịsịodee ọkpọọ bụzi ihe a tụlagara n'akụkụ anaghịzikwa eji ya ede ihe mgbe niile.
translations.reference: Sadly, as newer methods of writing have emerged, the pencil has been relegated to lesser status and uses.
translations.hypothesis: It is remarkable how a new method of communication, such as the use of a "keyboard," has emerged, allowing people to express themselves in ways that were previously impossible.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ na-edezi ozi na ihuenyo kọmputa gasị, o nweghị mgbe ha na-enwe ịbịaru nso na otu ọmụ nkọ.
translations.reference: People now write messages on computer screens, never having to come close to a sharpener.
translations.hypothesis: People are using computer screens to display information, and they are often able to see the same content at the same time.

translations.source: Mmadụ ga na-atụ naanị n’uche ihe kiibọọdụ ga-abụzi mgbe ihe kara dị ọhụrụ bịaziri.
translations.reference: One can only wonder what the keyboard will become when something newer comes along.
translations.hypothesis: People only expect growth when new investments are made.

translations.source: Bọmbụ fishọn ahụ na-arụ ọrụ n’iwu na ọ na ewere ike ijikọta otu nuclus ya na ọtụtụ protọnụ na nutrọnụ.
translations.reference: The fission bomb works on the principle that it takes energy to put together a nucleus with many protons and neutrons.
translations.hypothesis: The boron atom has an unusual structure and can form bonds with one electron and several protons and neutrons.

translations.source: Dika ibinggasi ugbo-ala nke di elu.Nkewa dị na etiti na elụ wee wepụta ike ụfọdụ.
translations.reference: Sort of like rolling a heavy cart up a hill. Splitting the nucleus up again then releases some of that energy.
translations.hypothesis: It is a type of tall, herbaceous plant. It has leaves that are arranged in pairs and produce flowers.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ atọm nwere nukei na-anọsighị ike nke pụtara na ha na-agbajikarị n'iji obere ma ọ bụ n'enweghị akwamaka.
translations.reference: Some atoms have unstable nuclei which means that they tend to break apart with little or no nudging.
translations.hypothesis: Some atoms have a nucleus that is unstable, meaning that they are likely to decay by emitting a particle.

translations.source: Elu ọnwa bụ ụmụ okwute na ájá mejupụtara ya. Mkpuchi mpụga ọnwa ka a na-akpọ krọstụ.
translations.reference: The surface of the Moon is made of rocks and dust. The outer layer of the Moon is called the crust.
translations.hypothesis: The full moon is a bright, round celestial body. The crescent moon is also known as the waning moon.

translations.source: Crọstụ ahụ dị ihe dị ka km70 n'ịgba agba n'akụkụ ya dị nso na km100 n'ịgba ịgba n'akụkụ ya tere anya.
translations.reference: The crust is about 70 km thick on the near side and 100 km thick on the far side.
translations.hypothesis: The coastline is approximately 70 kilometers long on one side and 100 kilometers long on the other side.

translations.source: Ọ kara taa ahụ n'okpuru marịa ma kara gbaa agba n'okpuru ụmụ ala ugwu ugwu ahụ.
translations.reference: It is thinner under the maria and thicker under the highlands.
translations.hypothesis: It is found growing beneath the railway tracks and also in the fertile soil of the surrounding hills.

translations.source: E nwere ike nwekwuo marịa ọzọ n'akụkụ ya dị nso n'ihi na krọstụ ya kara taa ahụ. Ọ kara dịrị mfe maka lava ịrịgote n'elu ya ahụ.
translations.reference: There may be more maria on the near side because the crust is thinner. It was easier for lava to rise up to the surface.
translations.hypothesis: It could have easily fallen over because of the uneven surface. It was very unstable and difficult to stand on.

translations.source: Tiori ndịnà bụ ndị a gbadoro anya ha ịchọta ihe na-eme ndị mmadụ kpaa agwa ha na-akpa ma ọ bụ ihe na-amasị ha.
translations.reference: Content theories are centered on finding what makes people tick or appeals to them.
translations.hypothesis: The tourists are looking for interesting and unique experiences that will give them a taste of local culture and traditions.

translations.source: Tiori ndị a na-ekwu na ndị mmadụ nwere mkpa ụfọdụ na/ma ọ bụ ọchịchọ nke ndị e chechala ma tinye n'uche dị ka ha na-etozuru ntorọbịa.
translations.reference: These theories suggest that people have certain needs and/or desires which have been internalized as they mature to adulthood.
translations.hypothesis: These theories suggest that people have a need or desire to understand and incorporate the experiences and perspectives of others.

translations.source: Tiori ndị a na-eleba anya n'ihe gbasara ụfọdụ ndị mmadụ nke kpatara ha ji achọ ihe ndị ha chọrọ na kedu ụmụ ihe nọ na gburugburu ebe obibi ha ga-eme ha mee ma ọ bụ emela ụfọdụ ihe.
translations.reference: These theories look at what it is about certain people that make them want the things that they do and what things in their environment will make them do or not do certain things.
translations.hypothesis: These theories explore the various factors that influence people's choices, including their desires, the environment in which they live, and the specific goods or services they are considering.

translations.source: Uzo-echiche ihe-di_n’ime abuo ama ama bu uzo-echiche ogogo nke mkpa nke Maslow na uzo-echiche ihe abuo kpatara nke Hertzberg.
translations.reference: Two popular content theories are Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory and Hertzberg's Two Factor Theory.
translations.hypothesis: The core concepts of Maslow's hierarchy of needs and Herzberg's two-factor theory.

translations.source: Ikwu n'izugbe, akparamaagwa abụọ nwere ike ịpụta dịka ndị  nlekọta na-amalite idu ndị ọgbọ ha ochie. Otu mpaghara n'echiche ahụ bụ "ịgbalị ịnọrọ dịka otu n'ime ụmụokorọbịa" (maọbụ ụmụagbọghọbịa).
translations.reference: Generally speaking, two behaviors can emerge as managers begin to lead their former peers. One end of the spectrum is trying to remain “one of the guys” (or gals).
translations.hypothesis: In the early stages of development, two siblings may appear to be identical twins. One area of this phenomenon is the "illusion of sameness" (also known as "twinship illusion").

translations.source: Ụdịrị onye njikwa a nwere ihe isi ike ime mkpebi ndị amasịghị, ime omume ndị ịdọ aka na ntị, ụmụ nnyocha arụmọrụ, ikenye ibu ọrụ, na ijide ndị mmadụ maka ịza ajụjụ nke ọrụ ha.
translations.reference: This type of manager has difficulty making unpopular decisions, performing disciplinary action, performance evaluations, assigning responsibility, and holding people accountable.
translations.hypothesis: This position involves making key decisions, implementing effective strategies, managing a team of analysts, ensuring the quality of work, and holding individuals accountable for their performance.

translations.source: Na njedebe ọzọ nke ụdị ahụ, otu onye ahụ ga-aghọ wụrụ mmadụ a na agali amata nke na- eche na ọ ga-agbanwerịrị ihe niile otu ahụ na- eme ma mee ka ọ bụrụ nke ha.
translations.reference: At the other end of the spectrum, one morphs into an unrecognizable individual that feels he or she must change everything the team has been doing and make it their own.
translations.hypothesis: This is another type of deception, where one person pretends to be someone else in order to gain trust and manipulate others, ultimately taking advantage of their vulnerability and exploiting their situation.

translations.source: Kaosiladị, onye ndu ahụ bụ ya ka ọ dịịrị n'ikpeazụ ịhụ maka ọdịmma na ọdịda nke òtù ahụ.
translations.reference: After all, the leader is ultimately responsible for the success and failure of the team.
translations.hypothesis: The leader, who is ultimately responsible for the well-being and success of the group,

translations.source: Gburugburu Medina ochie ahụ ọ dị mfe ịchọta ebe ndị na-ere ụmụ ngwaahịa ọdịnala Ndị Moroko, dị ka ụmụ tagịnị, ite akpụrụ akpụ, ngwaahịa ejiri akpụkpọ anụ mee, huuka, na giigawụ nke ụdịdị dị iche iche zuru ezu, mana ha nille bụ maka ndị nleta.
translations.reference: Around the old Medina it's easy to find places selling traditional Moroccan goods, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and a whole spectrum of geegaws, but it's all for the tourists.
translations.hypothesis: The old Medina market is easy to find, and it's full of traditional Moroccan crafts, such as carpets, pottery, leather goods, and various types of clothing. However, most of the vendors are elderly.

translations.source: Goma bụ obodo nleta nke Democratic Replublic nke Kongo n'ime akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ kachasị anya na nso Rwanda.
translations.reference: Goma is a tourist city of the Democratic Republic of Congo in the extreme east near Rwanda.
translations.hypothesis: Goma is a city in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, located in the eastern part of the country, near the border with Rwanda.

translations.source: N'afọ 2002, ebibiri Goma site n’aka lava si na ugwu ọkụ Nyiragongo nke liri ọtụtụ n'okporoama obodo, ọ kachasị etiti obodo.
translations.reference: In 2002 Goma was destroyed by lava from the Nyiragongo volcano which buried most of the town’s streets, particularly the town centre.
translations.hypothesis: In 2002, Goma was devastated by a volcanic eruption that flowed from the Nyiragongo crater down into the city, causing widespread destruction.

translations.source: Dịka Goma nwetụrụ nchekwa n’ụdị dịtụ mma, nleta ọ bụla na mpụga Goma bụ nke ekwesịrị inyocha iji ghọta ọnọdụ nke ọgụ ka nogidesiri ike n’Ugwu ngalaba ọchịchị kizu.
translations.reference: While Goma is reasonably safe, any visits outside of Goma should be researched to understand the state of the fighting that persists in the North Kivu province.
translations.hypothesis: Similar to how a well-maintained security system can prevent unauthorized access, any potential vulnerability in the Goma system should be carefully examined to identify and address any security risks that could compromise the integrity of the government's operations.

translations.source: Obodo ahụ bụkwa ntọala ịrị ugwu mgbawa Nyiragongo tinyere ụfọdụ nsochi Ọzọdimgba Ugwu dịchasị ọnụ ala n'Afrịka.
translations.reference: The city is also the base to climb the Nyiragongo volcano along with some of the cheapest Mountain Gorilla tracking in Africa.
translations.hypothesis: The area is also known as the Nyiragongo lava field, which includes part of the Virunga Mountains and is located in East Africa.

translations.source: Ị nwere ike iji boda-boda (tagzi ọgba tum tum) ịga gburugburu Goma. Ọnụahịa nkịtị (ebeụlọ) bụ Francs Ndị Congo ~500 maka ọkwụkwọ dị mkpirikpi.
translations.reference: You can use boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) to get around Goma. The normal (local) price is ~500 Congolese Francs for the short ride.
translations.hypothesis: You can use a taxi (often called a "matatu") to travel around Goma. A typical fare (per person) is around 500 Congolese Francs for a short trip.

translations.source: Tinyere na ira-ahu na nweta ya karia ibe ya, "Timbuktu" aburula ihe eji ama-atu maka ala ndi di anya, di oke-onu.
translations.reference: Combined with its relative inaccessibility, "Timbuktu" has come to be used as a metaphor for exotic, distant lands.
translations.hypothesis: Tinyere, a small child, was exploring her surroundings, "Timbuktu," a place known for its vibrant colors and bustling marketplace.

translations.source: Taa, Timbuktu obodo agụọ na-egbu, agbanyeghị n'ugwu ya na-eme ya otu ndọta ndị nleta, na o nwere otu ọdụ ụgbọelu.
translations.reference: Today, Timbuktu is an impoverished town, although its reputation makes it a tourist attraction, and it has an airport.
translations.hypothesis: Now, Timbuktu, the ancient city of learning, stands proudly on its hill, its buildings reflecting the wisdom of its scholars, and it has its own airport.

translations.source: N'afọ 1990, e debanyere ya n'etiti ebe ọpụrụiche n'ụwa ndị nọ na nsogbu mkpochapụ, maka nsogbu aja si n'ọzara.
translations.reference: In 1990, it was added to the list of world heritage sites in danger, due to the threat of desert sands.
translations.hypothesis: In 1990, he was brought to the forefront as a leading figure in the global fight against desertification, due to his expertise in this area.

translations.source: Ọ bụ otu isi nkwụsịtụ n'oge Henry Louis Gates Ihe-ebube pụrụ iche PBS nke Ụwa Afrịka.
translations.reference: It was one of the major stops during Henry Louis Gates' PBS special Wonders of the African World.
translations.hypothesis: It was a significant episode in the Henry Louis Gates Jr. special series on African-American history on PBS.

translations.source: Obodo ahụ dị n'ọdịiche kachasị ya n'ụmụ obodo nke mba ahụ fọdụrụnụ, n'ihi na o nwere karịa mmasị nke Arabik karịa otu Onye Afrịka.
translations.reference: The city is in stark contrast to the rest of the country's cities, because it has more of an Arabic flair than of an African.
translations.hypothesis: The city is known for its strong Arab influence, which is more pronounced than in any other part of the country.

translations.source: Obianụọhịa Kemba Kruger (KNP) nọ n'ebe ugwu-ọwụwa anyanwu nke South Afrịka ma nọrọ ogologo ókè ahụ nke Mozambik n'ime ọwụwa anyanwụ, Zimbabwe n'ime ebe ugwu, na ókè ebe ndịda ahụ bụ Osimmiri Agụiyi.
translations.reference: The Kruger National Park (KNP) lies in the north-east of South Africa and runs along the border of Mozambique in the east, Zimbabwe in the north, and the southern border is the Crocodile River.
translations.hypothesis: Obianụọhịa Kemba Kruger (KNP) is located in the southeastern part of South Africa and extends into Mozambique to the east, Zimbabwe to the north, and the neighboring areas of Mozambique.

translations.source: Ogige a ruru 19,500 km² nakwa ekewara ya n'ụzọ mpaghara ecozone 14, ebe nke ọbụla na-akwado ụdịrị anụ ọhịa dị iche.
translations.reference: The park covers 19,500 km² and is divided in 14 different ecozones, each supporting different wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: The area covers 19,500 square kilometers and is located within ecological zone 14, which supports a variety of animal species.

translations.source: Ọ bụ otu n’ime nke isi ihe ndọta nke Ndịda Afrịka ma a na-ewe ya dị ka nke kacha mma nke Ebennọkọta Nkeobodo (SANParks) Ndịda Afrịka.
translations.reference: It is one of the main attractions of South Africa and it is considered the flagship of South African National Parks (SANParks).
translations.hypothesis: It is one of the most important attractions of the African Wildlife, and is considered to be the best of the Kruger National Park (SANParks) in Africa.

translations.source: Dịka o si adị n'ogige mba niile nọ na Sawụtụ Afrịka, e nwere ụgwọ nchekwa n mbanye a na-akwụ kwa ụbọchị n'ogige a.
translations.reference: As with all South African National Parks, there are daily conservation and entry fees for the park.
translations.hypothesis: As is the case in many countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, there is a daily fee for using this particular public transportation system.

translations.source: O nwekwara ike iba uru ka mmadu gote Kaadi Ohia nke ga-enye gi ikikere iji banye na ogige ahoputagoro na South Africa ma o bu na Ogige Kemba South Africa niile.
translations.reference: It may also be beneficial for one to buy a Wild Card, which provides entry to either selections of parks in South Africa or all of the South African National Parks.
translations.hypothesis: It has the power to unlock the potential of individuals to access affordable healthcare in South Africa and also to provide access to quality healthcare services throughout South Africa.

translations.source: Ọ bụ site na Agwaetiti Họng Kọng ka mpaghara Họng Kọng nwetara aha ya; Ọ bụkwa ebe a ka ndị njem nlereanya na-ahụta dịka ebe kachasị mkpa.
translations.reference: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus.
translations.hypothesis: The area, known as Hong Kong, gained prominence due to its strategic location; and it remains a vital hub for trade and commerce.

translations.source: E jirila ụmụ ogologo ụlọ elu na-achọ igwe Họng Kọng mma maa atụ na ha yiri eserese baa chat, nke mmiri Viktoria Habọ mere ka ọ pụta ihe.
translations.reference: The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour.
translations.hypothesis: There are several tall buildings in Victoria Habo that have excellent views of the Họng Kọng, and they are all made of materials that reflect light, making them appear bright.

translations.source: Ịhụta Họng Kọng n'ụzọ kachasị mma, pụọ n'agwaetiti gawa na Kowloon, mpaghara akụkụ mmiri, nke chere gị ihu.
translations.reference: To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite.
translations.hypothesis: Experiencing the vibrant atmosphere of Hong Kong, particularly in the bustling waterfront district of Kowloon, is an unforgettable experience.

translations.source: Oke ihe ka n'ọnụ ọgụgụ n'ime mmepe obodo nke Agwaetiti Hong Kong jupụtara n'ọnụ na ala a napụtara na mmiri dị n'ogologo ụzọ nke ugwu akụkụ oke osimiri.
translations.reference: The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore.
translations.hypothesis: The impressive rock formation within the Hong Kong cityscape is located on a small island in the middle of the harbor, surrounded by a long, winding path of water.

translations.source: Ebe a bụ ebe ndị nchịkwa mba si Britenụ were dịka nke ha ya mere ọ bụrụ na ị na-achọ maka akaebe nke nchịkwa ókèala ahụ gara aga, ebe a bụ ebe dị mma ịmalite.
translations.reference: This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
translations.hypothesis: This is where government officials from Britain would have come to see the progress of the previous administration, and it is a good place to start.

translations.source: Ebe Sundarbans bụ ebe ala nwere ọhịa mmiri nọ n'akụkụ mmiri kachasị ukwuu n'ụwa dum, na-agbatị ruo kilomita 80 (50 mi) n'ime n'ala Bangladesh na India ahụ nke amaghị ama site n'ụsọ osimiri.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans are the largest littoral mangrove belt in the world, stretching 80 km (50 mi) into the Bangladeshi and Indian hinterland from the coast.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans is a vast mangrove forest, the largest in the world, stretching for 80 kilometers (50 miles) inland within the Bangladesh and Indian portions of the Bay of Bengal.

translations.source: E kwupụtawo na Sundarbans bụ otu Ebe Nketa Keụwa UNESCO. Akụkụ nke oke ọhịa n'ime ókèala nke Indịa ka a na-akpọ Obianụọhịa Kemba Sundarbans.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The part of the forest within Indian territory is called Sundarbans National Park.
translations.hypothesis: I have learned that the Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This is a mangrove forest located in the Ganges Delta of India, known as the Sundarbans Delta.

translations.source: Ọhịa ndị a abụghịkwa sọọsọ apịtị mangrov dị na ha – ha gụnyekwara ihe ndị ka fọrọ site n'oke ọhịa ndị juburu Ala nọ na mpaghara Ganjiz.
translations.reference: The forests aren't just mangrove swamps though — they include some of the last remaining stands of the mighty jungles which once covered the Gangetic plain.
